# Risks

Medium. This adds 18 PostgreSQL migrations and a narrowly marked nontransactional migration mode for online concurrent indexes. A defect could rewrite existing data, block hot writers, admit forged work, or publish the wrong index identity. The implementation keeps each schema migration below 100 lines, validates exact PostgreSQL-canonical index definitions and OIDs, fails closed on incomplete remnants without live-table repair DDL, and publishes markers plus the migration ledger only after final table/index locks and post-lock identity/ownership checks.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

This PR adds the durable authority required before a fair backup scheduler can enroll or claim work:

- write-once sandbox and node source identity plus snapshot visibility fencing;
- frozen enrollment cohorts, monotonic claim turns, priority passes, and shard authorities;
- tenant-bound admission work with explicit queued/deferred/leased/settled states, replay identity, lease fencing, and guarded deletion;
- durable queued-to-leased admission proofs bound to the exact transaction, cycle, shard, pass, attempt, high-water mark, and live lease before a claim cycle can restart;
- bounded claim/deferred/expired-lease indexes and exact hot-catalogue lane-conflict indexes;
- an explicit one-statement `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` migration path with canonical definition checks, fail-closed crash remnants, same-name race rejection, final publication locks, and atomic marker/ledger publication;
- Drizzle schema parity and full account-deletion FK classification;
- metadata-only GC admission reuse without rewriting existing GC rows.

There is intentionally no production repository, producer, caller, or `agent_backup_admission_work` insertion in this slice. The next enrollment PR is the first producer and must settle all admission work before irreversible account deletion. The following claim PR owns the 10,000-due-agent drain/fairness and zero-oversubscription proof.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature foundation and database integrity improvement.

# Documentation changes needed?

No user-facing documentation changes in this schema-only slice. Runtime activation and operator documentation belong to the later caller/deployment slice.

45:T273a,# feat(billing): expose provider-neutral payment states in billing UI

Closes #22966

## What this does

Extends the Billing surface with a server-authoritative, read-only projection of purchase payment states — unifying #22427's provider-neutral receipts, Stripe checkout orders, and the refund/dispute clawback+reinstatement credit ledger:

- **`PaymentHistoryService.listPaymentStates`** (`packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/payment-history.ts`): org-scoped projection with typed purchase identity (Stripe payment-intent unification; OxaPay joins via `payment_request_id` — synthetic grant keys can never collide with a real Stripe intent, so no cross-provider reversal leakage).
- **`GET /api/v1/billing/payment-states`** (`packages/cloud/api/v1/billing/payment-states/route.ts`): org-auth + standard rate limit, bounded pagination, J1 boundary translation.
- **`PaymentActivityCard`** (`packages/ui/src/cloud/billing/components/payment-activity-card.tsx`): distinct loading / empty / error-with-retry / success / unavailable states; status never conveyed by color alone (icon + verbatim state text); credit amounts labeled as credits, never formatted as currency. Each row links to its payment detail.
- **Linked order/receipt detail (#22966 review r3–r5)**: `GET /api/v1/billing/payment-states/:id` (org-scoped lookup over the same projection — id validated (`{surface}:{authority}` shape, length ≤ 200) before any service call; real 404 when the row is outside the org's bounded history window; lossless offset paging since r5 — see the superseded r4 note below) + `cloud/billing/payments/:id` (`PaymentStateDetailPage`, registered specific-before-general) with loading / not-found / error-with-retry / success states, full-shape payload validation (a partial row is an explicit error, never a fabricated render), typed `ApiError.status === 404` branching, and the full identifiers (not truncated) with copy affordances + J4 clipboard degrade.

### Authority model

| Fact | Authority |
|---|---|
| Settled purchase (amount, currency, provider, settlement time) | immutable `payment_request_receipts` row (#22427) |
| Settled request without receipt | explicit `unavailable` — never a fabricated success |
| Legacy checkout orders (no receipt possible) | durable server order row |
| Refund/dispute cumulative USD | per-authority max snapshot (charge.id / dispute.id), then summed across authorities — Stripe's cumulative semantics, no replay double-count |
| Applied clawback / reinstatement | credit units (ledger row amounts), kept separate from provider USD |
| Unrecovered balance shortfall | explicit amber line from the clawback mutation's recorded shortfall |
| Policy effect | always `unavailable` + reason while #22930 (refund entitlement policy) is unresolved — never a guessed outcome |
| Reversal association | receipt `provider` + `provider_tx_ref` when a receipt exists (immutable); mutable request row is legacy fallback only |

### Tests (all green at head)

- **44 pglite service tests** (`payment-history.pglite.test.ts`, 413 `expect()` calls) — real schema, real SQL: base states incl. `expired`, org isolation, provider isolation (OxaPay↔Stripe), replay (unique ledger index rejects duplicate insert — DrizzleQueryError cause-chain walk, probe-proven), partial-after-consumption, dispute withdraw→reinstate ordering, two-tab checkout, lost post-payment response, receipt-vs-request divergence (amount/currency/time AND reversal association), stale-ref non-attachment control.
- **21 UI vitest tests** across `payment-activity-card.test.tsx` (row links: exact `href` + action-specific accessible names under a real router) and `PaymentStateDetailPage.test.tsx` (loading / not-found / error+retry / malformed / partial-payload drop-one-field ×8 / full-row rendering / copy identifiers / reversal totals / no-receipt honesty).
- **8 route tests** across `payment-states-detail-route.test.ts` + `payment-states-list-route.test.ts` — org's own row by stable projection id, 404 outside the window, tenant isolation (ORG_A vs ORG_B), 400 on malformed ids before any service call.
- Full billing UI directory regression: **17 files / 286 tests green** at head.

Closes #24371

Replaces the removed third-party proxy transport with direct first-party WeChat paths: Official Account (MP) and WeCom self-built apps over the official platform APIs — signature-verified public callback server, official customer-service/app-message sends, no proxy.

## What changes

- **Direct transports** — `api-client.ts` / `token-manager.ts` (account-scoped access tokens, single-flight) send through fixed `api.weixin.qq.com` / `qyapi.weixin.qq.com` hosts; personal/proxy/wecom-third-party modes rejected with typed errors; legacy `WECHAT_API_KEY`/`WECHAT_PROXY_URL` fail with `WECHAT_PROXY_CONFIG_UNSUPPORTED`.
- **Callback boundary** — `callback-server.ts` + `callback-crypto.ts`: SHA-1 signature verification before any parsing; AES-256-CBC encrypted mode with Tencent's 32-byte PKCS#7 scheme; receiver-id binding (corpId / gh_ original ID — never appId); per-account path addressing so a ciphertext signed for one account is never accepted for another.
- **Hardened XML** — `xml.ts` flat parser (CDATA leaves, no DTD/entities/nesting/duplicate roots), parsed only after signature verification.
- **Connector + account provider** — targets derived exclusively from signature-verified inbound senders (no roster API on these platforms); observational account status (connected requires a real first-party observation).
- **Tests** — 16 new tests across 6 suites (config resolution, callback boundary with real listeners, crypto with official Tencent vectors, UTF-8 chunk-boundary integrity, token lifecycle, provider), all with RED controls per review round.

## Key invariants

- Signature verification precedes payload parsing; encrypted-mode accounts cannot be downgraded to the plaintext path by request shape.
- Outbound receipts are enforced: platform rejection, non-zero errcode, or unparseable body is a failed send — never a fabricated success.
- Replay expiry aligns with the timestamp freshness endpoint (r5 fix).

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Preserves locally owned optimistic message lineage after terminal receipts replace temporary row IDs. A stale independently running history request can therefore merge without deleting the just-rekeyed user and assistant rows; later durable history still converges without duplicates.

The source fix is deliberately narrow: local ownership now follows a temporary `id` **or** a preserved temporary `clientRenderId`. Conversation ownership and server-ID deduplication remain unchanged. The PR also extends the deterministic browser regression fixture and its CI workflow coverage.

# Risks

Medium, isolated to database schema and the not-yet-consumed replacement-attempt repository surface. The migration adds an owner-lifetime append-only authority table, constraints, partial unique indexes, immutability/state-transition triggers, and a composite foreign key to the exact append-only Docker-node occurrence.

The occurrence tuple is `(history id, Docker-node record id, node incarnation)`, rather than the incarnation UUID alone, so node rotation and ABA reuse fail closed. Direct row deletion and truncation remain forbidden. An organization-owned cascade is allowed only for terminal non-restore history; active replacement effects abort the entire organization deletion. Existing restore-backed retention authorities can still reject organization deletion.

This PR does not deploy or apply the migration to a live database. If #25372 or the migration tail changes first, this branch must be restacked, renumbered, and revalidated before merge.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Adds the missing SQL migration and journal registration for the already-defined `agent_sandbox_replacement_attempts` schema/repository, then binds every durable replacement locator to one exact Docker-node occurrence.

The table:

- fences duplicate provider effects by active agent and activation generation;
- binds optional restore-lease provenance;
- enforces complete locator and receipt shapes;
- preserves the exact node occurrence across rotation and ABA reuse;
- revalidates and locks the current Docker-node occurrence before placement/adoption;
- retains attempt history for the owner's lifetime;
- permits terminal non-restore erasure only through the owning organization cascade, while unresolved/provider-succeeded effects block that erasure atomically.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature / database migration substrate.

# Documentation changes needed?

No external documentation change is required. The migration, repository contract, and tests document the state machine and authority tuple directly; runtime consumption will be reviewed separately.

# Risks

Traffic fence is deliberately fail-open for scopes with no installation record (existing installs keep working); only terminal-state records (`removed`/`revoked`/`failed`) stop traffic, which is exactly the issue criterion ("removal stops traffic"). Scope-creep guard: no database migration, no API routes, no UI changes.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Implements the first tranche of the canonical invite-to-ready group installation lifecycle (#23107):

1. **Durable provider-neutral state machine** (`packages/core/src/messaging/installation-lifecycle.ts`): an account-scoped installation record joining provider invite, external group, required scopes, single-use expiring owner claim, runtime room binding, readiness state, removal, and reinstall versioning. States: `invite_created → provider_authorized → agent_joined → permissions_verifying → owner_claim_pending → ready`, with terminal `degraded`/`removed`/`revoked`/`failed`. Signed-event normalization: events are tenant-bound, idempotent, replay-safe (terminal receipt replay is a no-op), and epoch-guarded (future `reinstallVersion` epochs rejected; stale epochs rejected; equal-epoch reapply rejects wrong-secret attempts and persists attempt burning to exhaustion).
2. **Connector contribution contract** (`packages/core/src/messaging/installation-contribution.ts` + `installation-service.ts`): the contract a connector implements — install/deep-link shape, group types, scope requirements, signed event normalization, readiness proof, uninstall, provider-specific activation. `InstallationLifecycleService` registers contributions per `(agentId, connectorId)`.
3. **Discord pilot adapter** (`plugins/plugin-discord/installation-adapter.ts`, `discord-events.ts`, `index.ts`, `messages.ts`): canonical permission catalog (tiered invite URL activation), guildCreate/guildDelete normalization (unknown shapes refused), owner-claim handoff that never exposes tokens in the group, and the gateway-boundary fence — a fenced (removed/revoked/failed) guild skips `handleGuildCreate` at the event-listener seam and stops message traffic at the message-send seam.

## What kind of change is this?

Features (non-breaking change which adds functionality).

# Documentation changes needed?

My changes do not require a change to the project documentation (contract is documented in code headers; user-facing install UX arrives with the next tranche's install-URL surface).

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

1. `packages/core/src/messaging/installation-lifecycle.test.ts` — 49 tests over the state machine: legal transitions, replay/idempotency, claim single-use + expiry + attempt burning, epoch guards, removal semantics.
2. `plugins/plugin-discord/__tests__/installation-adapter.test.ts` — contribution shape (permission catalog, tiered invite URLs), event normalization (unknown shapes refused), traffic gate semantics.
3. `plugins/plugin-discord/__tests__/installation-gateway-boundary.test.ts` — the fence at the real `setupDiscordEventListeners` seam: a fenced guild never reaches `handleGuildCreate`.
4. `plugins/plugin-discord/__tests__/installation-contribution-init.test.ts` — plugin init registers the contribution against the real core service.

56:T177c,## Summary

Closes #22961. Adds a single settlement authority for MCP purchases: one authoritative receipt row per economic event, first-committed-wins with replay-mismatch rejection, every payout leg applied exactly once under settlement-scoped idempotency keys, and a durable recovery lane on the credit-reservation cron that resumes wedged receipts and refunds orphaned precharges.

- `mcp_settlements` receipt table: `(payment_type, payment_event_id)` is the canonical identity of one purchase; replay of the same event lands on the committed row, replay with different economics throws.
- Every leg (creator org credit, creator redeemable earnings, affiliate earnings, usage row + stats) keys its idempotency on the settlement receipt, so re-driving a delivery — retry, concurrent duplicate, or sweep resume — is exactly-once.
- Claim-timestamp ownership protocol on the buyer debit (`mcp_precharge_swept` + `mcp_precharge_swept_at`): the live delivery and the recovery sweep claim the same row through mutually exclusive single-row UPDATEs; staleness is judged by when the claim was written, never by the debit's age; a failed sweep refund stays retryable until the refund commits; the deducting `recordUsage` path tags its debit for the same recovery.
- Balanced-ledger suite proves conservation of value across retries, concurrent delivery, crash-recovery, sweep/late-delivery races, and refund-retry — 23 tests, each new race RED-proven against the prior commit before being fixed.

## What is deliberately NOT changed

The dual creator-credit legs (creator org credit + creator redeemable earnings from one purchase) are preserved exactly as they behave today — no money flow is altered by this PR. The open economic-policy question was posted on the issue (2026-08-23): each leg is independently keyed to the receipt, so a ruling to drop one leg is a one-line change gated on the same linkage. Tracking: #22942 parent audit.

## Evidence

- Balanced-ledger suite: `bun test --isolate ./packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/__tests__/mcp-settlement-balanced-ledger.test.ts` — 23/23 pass, covering single delivery, retry, concurrent duplicate, unkeyed settlement, replay mismatch, partial-leg recovery, sweep refund of orphans, late-delivery-after-refund refusal, crashed-live-claim redelivery, dead-claim reclaim after horizon, stale-claim vs sweep race, refunding-window refusal, failed-refund retry-exactly-once, deducting-path crash recovery, and the mid-delivery sweep race on an old debit.
- Numeric conservation suite: `user-mcps-recordusage-numeric.test.ts` — 17/17 pass.
- RED controls (fix-removed, test-only runs at the prior commits): round-6 tests fail 3/3 on round-5 code; the round-7 mid-delivery race test fails on round-6 code (sweep refunds mid-delivery; delivery settles a refunded debit).
- Typecheck: `bun run --cwd packages/cloud/shared typecheck` exit 0; `bun run --cwd packages/cloud/api typecheck` exit 0.
- Lint: `biome check` clean on all changed files.
- Review: independent RepoPrompt-agent convergence review, 8 rounds; round-6 findings (stale-claim refund race, unretryable failed refund, unrecoverable deducting-path debit) and round-7 finding (live claim missing its timestamp stamp) each verified real, fixed, and RED-proven before approval at head 2a93127d0f.
- Pre-existing failure (not this PR): `agent-backup-restore-api-boundary.test.ts` fails identically on pristine develop at 126807701e (control run in a separate worktree) — `loadCurrentAgentVaultKeyAuthority must remain definition-only`.

# Risks

**Large safety surface, bounded activation risk.** This changes Docker replacement creation, exact cleanup/replay, Headscale identity cleanup, registry ambiguity tracking, and attempt-scoped secret transport. # Background

## What does this PR do?

- Advertises an `exact-success` replacement capability with a caller-owned, one-shot UUID and ordered start → intent → Docker-created → VPN-enriched → success-only settlement callbacks.
- Freezes exact Docker-node authority as the immutable DB record UUID plus hostname, SSH port/user, and host-key pin; replay resolves on the primary by record UUID and rejects authority drift before SSH.
- Adds a remote `flock`/tombstone protocol, active-producer marker, durable candidate-ID receipt, and deterministic cleanup of six temporary secret paths. Ambiguous or late Docker outcomes remain fenced.
- Makes exact Headscale cleanup ID-authoritative with strict inventory proof and binds the API registration IP to the exact Docker container's Tailscale IP.
- Tracks ambiguous registry/autoscale completion and prevents a success callback after unresolved remote mutation.
- Preserves the real legacy `ElizaSandboxService` intent/created/VPN callback contract without requiring the new exact tuple.

If an exact locator has a Docker container ID and Headscale registration metadata but no durable Headscale node ID, cleanup remains `in_flight_unresolved`; polling by name cannot prove absence against a late Headscale POST. If Docker start was never reached (`containerId === null` under the strict stage contract), cleanup can safely omit Headscale.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix and provider-side prerequisite for the remaining #22947 admission work.

# Documentation changes needed?

No external documentation change is required. The public provider types contain the exact consumer contract and explicitly state that Slice S must add durable consumer persistence, append-only migration, node-authority revalidation/locking, and the final CAS.

<!-- eliza-computer-attribution:v1 {"provider":"openai","model":"gpt-5.6","client":"Codex Desktop","skill_revision":"N/A - contribution skill unavailable in this session"} -->59:T16d7,## What

Adds structural server management to the stock Discord connector, exposed through the production `MESSAGE` tool as `op=manage_server` (`source=discord`). This wires the previously declared-but-unimplemented `DiscordActionConfig` gates (`channels`, `roles`, `permissions`, `moderation`) to real, bounded operations so an agent can build and maintain a Discord server from ordinary chat instructions.

### Verbs

- `create_category`, `create_channel`, `edit_channel`, `delete_channel`
- `create_role`, `edit_role`, `delete_role`
- `edit_permissions` (channel permission overwrites, role/user/@everyone subject)
- `assign_role`, `remove_role`
- `create_invite`
- `kick`, `ban`, `unban`, `timeout`
- `list_templates`, `apply_template` (idempotent template reconcile)

## Security gates (fail closed)

- Every structural write requires the corresponding `settings.discord.actions.channels|roles|permissions|moderation` gate to be **explicitly `true`**. Absent config = OFF. Truthy non-boolean values (e.g. the string `"true"`) also stay OFF. Env fallbacks (`DISCORD_ACTIONS_*`) are consulted only when the config key is absent. `apply_template` requires channels + roles + permissions together.
- **Role hierarchy enforced**: only roles strictly below the bot's highest role can be edited/deleted/assigned; integration-managed roles and `@everyone` are refused; kick/ban/timeout honor `kickable`/`bannable`/`moderatable` and refuse the guild owner.
- **No admin bypass**: granting `Administrator` through any role or overwrite is always rejected, and requested permissions must be a subset of what the bot itself holds (no escalation).
- Guild/channel ownership validated (`CHANNEL_WRONG_GUILD`, `CHANNEL_NOT_FOUND`, `MEMBER_NOT_FOUND`); the bot's own Discord-side permission (`ManageChannels`, `ManageRoles`, `CreateInstantInvite`, `KickMembers`, `BanMembers`, `ModerateMembers`) is checked per verb with an actionable re-invite message.
- Bounded inputs: name/topic/permission-list/overwrite-count limits, hex color validation, invite age clamped to 7 days, timeout clamped to 28 days, ban delete-window clamped to 7 days. Unknown permission names are rejected by name. No tokens in any output.

## Non-destructive template reconcile

`apply_template` reconciles a declarative guild spec (roles -> categories -> channels -> overwrites, deterministic order) against the live guild:

- Objects match by **stable template key** via a persisted key->snowflake map (runtime cache, per account+guild+template), with exact-name fallback, so re-apply converges to `unchanged` instead of duplicating.
- Managed-field drift (name, topic, parent, color, hoist, mentionable, permissions, overwrites) is corrected; **unmanaged channels and roles are NEVER deleted**. Deletion exists only as the explicit gated `delete_channel`/`delete_role` verbs.
- `dryRun: true` returns the full plan (`would_create`/`would_update`) without touching Discord — on every verb, not just templates.
- Four vendor-neutral built-in templates ship as plugin assets: `companion-private`, `friends-casual`, `project-team`, `community-public`. Deployments extend/override via `settings.discord.guildTemplates` (per-account override supported). `{{agent}}` renders the character name.
- Every operation returns a structured receipt listing created/updated/unchanged/skipped entities plus a human summary.

## Tool path

`plugin-discord` still registers `actions: []`. The surface rides the existing message-connector contract:

- `packages/core/src/types/runtime.ts`: new optional `manageServerHandler` connector hook + `manage_server` capability + param/result types.
- `packages/core/src/features/advanced-capabilities/actions/message.ts`: new `manage_server` op with natural-language verb aliases (`create_channel`, `apply_template`, `kick_member`, ...), bounded param forwarding (allowlisted keys only), and `MESSAGE_PARAMETERS` schema entries for discoverability.
- `plugins/plugin-discord/service.ts`: `manageConnectorServer` adapts the live guild to the management module and registers the hook per account (multi-account scoping preserved).
- `plugins/plugin-discord/guild-management.ts` / `guild-templates.ts`: the management engine operates on narrow structural interfaces so tests drive it with plain fakes.

## Config defaults

```json
{
  "settings": {
    "discord": {
      "token": "<bot token>",
      "actions": { "channels": true, "roles": true, "permissions": true, "moderation": false }
    }
  }
}
```

Default remains everything OFF; the snippet above is the opt-in example documented in the README.

## Tests

- `plugins/plugin-discord/__tests__/guild-management.test.ts` (39 tests): gate-off denial per gate, hierarchy denial (role above bot, managed role, @everyone, non-kickable member, guild owner), Administrator/escalation rejection, malformed permissions/colors/ids, idempotent second apply (zero writes), reconcile-after-manual-rename, **no deletion of unmanaged objects**, dry-run plans (no writes, no state persistence), invite/timeout clamping, tenant template registry.
- `packages/core/src/features/advanced-capabilities/actions/message.manage-server.test.ts` (9 tests): alias routing, bounded forwarding (unknown params dropped), missing-operation and no-connector failures, gate denials surfacing as structured action failures, receipt passthrough.

Fixes #25518. Refs #25268, #26821, and #22896.5d:T18fc,# feat(core,plugin-sql): native paging for large messages and attachment text (#25140)

Closes #25140

Adds native content segmentation and paging so large message bodies and attachment text are stored as revision-fenced segments and paged on demand, instead of being written and read as single unbounded rows.

## What changes

- **`packages/core/src/memory/content-segmentation.ts` (new)** — segmentation contracts: bounded segment emission, surrogate-safe boundaries, deterministic segment identity; 14 unit tests.
- **`core memory.ts` / `types/database.ts`** — `getMemoryContentPage` paging read path; message/readAttachment actions consume pages instead of whole rows.
- **`plugin-sql` schema + store (new: `memoryTextSegments`)** — generation-addressed segments with revision fencing: `createMemory` publishes segments with a bounded marker, `updateMemory` replaces the generation and retires the stale one, large-to-small replacement retires the descriptor, deletion cascades; small content stays inline (fallback path returns null pages); large attachment text without an id or with duplicate ids is rejected.
- **Real-runtime suites (new)** — 10 real PGlite tests: parent-first publication, paging with revision fencing, reassembly across restart, atomic generation replacement, legacy large-unsegmented row flagging, owner-bound attachment paging, access-context probe coverage, rollback atomicity.

## Key invariants

- Pages are revision-fenced: a reader can never reassemble content mixing two generations.
- Generation replacement is atomic and retires the prior generation — stale segments are never served after an update.
- Legacy large unsegmented rows are flagged, not silently repaged; small rows pass through inline.

## Test-lane disclosure

Nine of the ten new plugin-sql tests live in `*.real.test.ts` files, which the PR vitest lane deliberately excludes (`plugins/plugin-sql/src/vitest.config.ts`, #10104) — they run on the post-merge lane (`VITEST_LANE=post-merge` / `TEST_LANE=post-merge`) and in the captures below. The pre-merge green checks therefore reflect the non-real suites (core unit + surface + probe tests), not the real-PGlite fencing behavior; see the backend-logs capture for the real-suite evidence. The post-merge lane does execute plugin-sql real suites.

No deploy is included or authorized by this Draft PR.60:T1b29,# feat(core,plugin-sql): durable lossless manifest shard ledger with restart-safe traversal (#25141)

Closes #25141

Introduces a durable, lossless content-manifest shard ledger so progressive content (trajectories and other paginated corpora) survives restarts and concurrent writers without truncation or orphaned shards.

Investigation doc: `docs/design/context-content/25141-manifest-shard-persistence-investigation.md` (included).

## What changes

- **`packages/core/src/runtime/content-manifest-ledger.ts` (new)** — generation-addressed shard writes with a rolling `chainSha256` over shard body bytes; `ManifestHead.contentSha256` retention-bound digest (createdAt-free); load-path digest verification with a typed integrity error; deterministic idempotency (content-digest comparison on both write paths); entry-level revision containment (`entryIdentity` = kind + reference + normalized revision, range-coverage superset check).
- **`packages/core/src/types/content-manifest-shards.ts` (new)** — shard type contracts: fixed-point byteLength measure, `CONTENT_MANIFEST_SHARD_DEFAULT_ENTRIES=64`, >maxBytes typed rejection.
- **`plugin-sql/src/base.ts`** — SQL CAS split into insert-only (`onConflictDoNothing`) vs conditional-update arms (ABA-safe); loser sweeps own generation; delete/clear sweeps ledger rows (`RETURNING id`).
- **`plugin-inmemorydb` + core `inMemoryAdapter`** — atomic CAS via document mutation lock; `compareAndSwapCache` contract with base-class default for structural third-party adapters.
- **`TrajectoriesService` / agent prune paths** — prune-delete guard via `contentManifestLedgerKeys` wired into `discard` and `pruneOldTrajectories` (RETURNING-id cleanup).
- **Tests** — 48 core ledger/shard unit tests, 11 real PGlite integration + restart tests (deterministic injected-clock runs, entry-level revision containment vectors, restart superset/grown-ranges manifest assertions).

## Key invariants

- A restart never publishes a shrinking manifest that silently drops recorded entries: the restart suite asserts superset/grown-ranges (a shrinking 5-replaces-9 manifest was found by a stash control and fixed).
- Idempotency compares content digests, not wall-clock timestamps; writer races resolve CAS-safe with loser-side sweep of its own generation.
- Load-path verifies the chain digest and fails with a typed integrity error rather than serving truncated content.

Relates to #24407. Depends on Draft #29662.

This is the repository-only enrollment producer. It does not activate a caller, claim/defer/settle work, invoke a provider, trigger autoscale, retire the legacy scheduler, or claim the 10,000-due-agent fairness acceptance.

- [x] This PR is intentionally stacked on `feat/24407-backup-admission-schema-v3` because it writes the authority introduced by #29662.
- [x] Exact base #29662 is merge-forwarded through current `origin/develop` with zero conflicts.
- [ ] Full-repository `bun run verify` was not rerun; exact affected validation is recorded below.

# Risks

Medium. Enrollment advances sandbox schedule state and creates durable backup work. A defect could skip due work, duplicate queue entries, cross a source occurrence, or strand a shard. The repository therefore uses one atomic transaction, frozen per-shard cohort authority, bounded disjoint candidate frontiers, exact source revalidation, deterministic organization locking, and replay-safe insertion.

# What does this PR do?

- Leases one of 64 durable enrollment shards with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, preferring incomplete cohorts.
- Freezes the database cutoff, snapshot xid, RPO, cohort identity, and keyset cursor for resumable enrollment.
- Selects three disjoint due frontiers, each bounded at `limit + 1`, then globally orders and caps the result.
- Revalidates active organization lifecycle and exact sandbox/node occurrence authority before mutation.
- Atomically advances `next_backup_at`, enrollment cursors, queued `schedule_capture` / `reserve_capture` work, and shard progress.
- Inserts exact replay identities with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`; queued rows begin with attempts `0`, no lease, and no claim proof.
- Performs database admission mutations only. It has no provider, provisioning, capacity, autoscale, or restore dependency.

# What this PR does

- Keeps browser and native Cloud request deadlines active through response body/decode work, propagates caller cancellation without replacing its reason/cause, and rechecks the absolute wall clock immediately before every transport dispatch.
- Starts the six-minute Dedicated startup deadline at `ensurePersonalDedicatedEliza()` entry, not after Personal/quote/activation preflight. Personal GET, quote GET, activation POST, bodies, reconciliation, and cutover polling all consume the same remaining budget.
- Proves a `359999 -> 360000` dispatch crossover sends zero late POSTs and that aggregate preflight + quote + ambiguous activation + cutover settles by 360000 ms with no late effects.
- Distinguishes direct session verification outcomes: only authoritative 401/403 may request reauthentication. Body stalls, malformed responses, 5xx, and transport failures retain the token and surface a transient retry outcome.
- Makes required-client-auth mounted Steward login fail closed on transient verification, matching Android behavior, so first-run join/provisioning cannot continue on an unverified retained token. Optional login UI still retains the token and shows a retry message.
- Recognizes retained Dedicated states without replay: `pending`, `provisioning`, and `running` reattach with zero activation POST; `error`, `stopped`, and `sleeping` allow exactly one fresh quote-bound same-target activation; unknown state and target mismatch fail closed.
- Uses stable `ElizaError` codes with sanitized context for invalid activation, unknown quote/status, and target mismatch.
- Guards Personal identity recovery diagnostics so a rejected diagnostic sink cannot mask the original typed recovery failure.
- Records a single fixed payload-free warning when that diagnostic sink rejects, while preserving the original typed failure; the J2/J4/J7 catch boundaries carry explicit repository-policy rationales.
- Retains privacy-safe counters only; no credentials, response payloads, account identifiers, or billing secrets are logged.

# Review remediation receipts

- `discussion_r3873629448`: response metadata now survives body rejection and timeout, including status, URL, response headers, and parsed `Retry-After`. The retained-target regression proves zero activation replay.

# Risks

Large if merged prematurely: this is a new concurrency and durability authority boundary. The current draft has no migration, journal entry, or runtime consumer, so it has no deployed behavior by itself and is intentionally not mergeable.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

This draft introduces the S1 durable substrate for one-shot sandbox replacement attempts:

- a tenant-scoped attempt schema that freezes caller attempt identity, activation/lifecycle authority, backup/restore authority, complete S0 node/SSH placement identity, monotonic locator enrichment, and byte-identical receipts;
- a global partial unique fence on `(organization_id, agent_id)` while an attempt is `in_flight_unresolved` or `provider_succeeded`;
- a per-generation partial unique fence that additionally retains `lifecycle_committed` history for the same activation generation;
- transaction-composable repository operations for start, intent, locator stages, provider success, lifecycle adoption, cleanup proof, and primary reads, with typed conflict/not-found/validation errors;
- adversarial PGlite coverage for real rotation, concurrency, rollback, replay, cleanup/start serialization, terminal immutability, tenant isolation, malformed authority, and non-expiring unresolved attempts.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature: a bounded backend persistence substrate for later #22947 runtime slices.

# Documentation changes needed?

N/A - the draft adds an internal schema/repository contract with inline API documentation and focused executable tests. Operator/deployment documentation must accompany the future migration/runtime integration, not this non-deployable draft.

## What changes

## Key invariants

- Partial/failed/intent-missing evidence reports `unavailable`/`incomplete`; it never implies removals.
- Per-account scoping: one account's degrade never marks another account's evidence stale.
- `conversations.replies` ordering is earliest-first (parent-first) per Slack docs — the harness previously asserted the reverse, which was a production bug fixed with a RED control.

6f:Tb88,## Cause

The Android and live-voice evidence paths could publish device serials, raw logcat/command diagnostics, provider/model/backend/provenance values, and captured physical/system audio through logs or uploaded artifacts. The `always()` upload paths could also expose partially written evidence, and the existing voice matrix v1 schema still carried raw diagnostic fields.

## Resolution

- project Android workflow output through a closed, allowlisted status/code boundary; keep serials, logcat, screenshots, raw console output, and runner state private
- bind published Android evidence to the exact revision/build identity and SHA-256 manifest; emit black, audio-free video only
- move voice evidence to `eliza_voice_live_matrix_v2` and remove raw host/filter/probe/child diagnostics
- derive public voice audio only as a fixed 997 Hz synthetic tone from duration; publish black video plus that projected tone, never captured mic/system audio
- stage, verify, and atomically rename the exact manifest-bound Android and voice artifact sets into absent destinations
- reject symlink destinations and parent substitution; pin and revalidate publication ancestry, parent, and staging identities
- keep the hosted Android bootstrap at `android/logs/` while atomically publishing its allowlisted proof at `android/evidence/`
- use the canonical per-user runner temp directory as the explicit Windows publication trust boundary, with a fresh absent default child
- isolate workflow roots by run id/attempt and make teardown sequential and bounded

## Verification

- `bun install --frozen-lockfile`
- targeted Android/voice suite: **64 passed, 1 intentional inverse-toolchain skip, 0 failed, 577 assertions**
- adversarial coverage includes destination and parent symlinks, destination/parent substitution, partial projection cleanup, untrusted POSIX ancestry, bootstrap/evidence coexistence, and manifest/hash verification
- `actionlint` on all edited workflows
- `shellcheck` and `bash -n` on the ARM64 preflight
- `node --check` on edited runtime scripts
- Biome: pass (three pre-existing string-literal warnings in `device-e2e-workflow.test.ts`)

No physical phone run, workflow dispatch, deployment, infrastructure mutation, or merge was performed.

## Review notes

The intentionally reduced diagnostics make failures less human-readable. Published audio is no longer a recording of the session; it proves only duration-bound media plumbing. Consumers must use the v2 matrix schema and the new artifact roles. Publication requires an absent destination. On Windows, an explicit output outside the canonical runner/user temp boundary fails closed.

Rollback is a single-commit revert.

Complementary: #29437, #29485  
Related tracking: #13580, #1693770:T1bc3,## Summary

Closes #28875.

Adds a durable compare-and-set cache primitive (`compareAndSetCache`) so
policy-shaped cache writes can be atomic at the shared backing store instead of
racing read-modify-write over `getCache`/`setCache` — the cross-process lost-update
window that exists during managed blue/green upgrades when two container
generations briefly share the durable cache.

**Stacked on #28750** (recipient-bound push delivery). Only the last 2 commits
are #28875 scope; the first 3 commits are #28750's and will drop out of this PR
when #28750 merges.

- `compareAndSetCache<T>(key, expected, replacement)` declared on the core
  runtime/cache contract (`IAgentRuntime`, `IDatabaseAdapter`) with
  `expected === undefined` = insert-only-if-absent, `false` = conflict
  (caller reloads and retries), typed `ElizaError` on storage failure.
- Production adapters implement it with atomic statements: plugin-sql
  (single `UPDATE ... WHERE` / transaction), plugin-inmemorydb,
  `InMemoryDatabaseAdapter` fallback (refuses rather than silently
  non-atomic for adapters that cannot guarantee CAS).
- `PushPolicyStore.update()` migrated to CAS-on-version with bounded conflict
  retry; `PushTokenRegistry` hydrate repair is itself a CAS against the raw
  baseline so a concurrent writer conflicts the repair instead of being
  overwritten.

73:T1ca4,## Summary

Closes #23453

Binds the restore drill's authority to the specific archive, authenticates RPO metadata, and scales the isolation proof to linear — through a signed, expiring, single-use restore capability enforced on the server clock at every destructive boundary.

### What changed

- **Archive-bound capability** (`restore-capability.ts`, new): HMAC-signed envelope binding `target_id` + archive sha256 + nonce, mint-time clamped TTL, single-use. The signature covers `issuedAt` so a re-signed grant cannot claim an older minting.
- **Dual-setting target authority**: the disposable target carries `eliza.restore_target_id` + `eliza.restore_capability` twins in `postgresql.auto.conf`; every guarded psql session re-checks both before its first statement, plus a **server-clock expiry check** (millisecond precision) derived from the signed bytes — no local-check/SQL-execution TOCTOU.
- **Claim ordering**: the transactional exclusivity claim persists **only after** the clean-target role-collision check passes; a refused first invocation leaves no claim, so a retry can never masquerade as a same-capability retry.
- **Session-held drill lock**: advisory-lock holder with a proven file handshake; the holder re-proves lock ownership before its hold-sleep (a DO block — a refused or dispossessed holder aborts instead of leaking a 24h `pg_sleep` backend); release terminates the holder backend gated on `pg_locks` proving the pid still holds this exact lock (PID-reuse safe).
- **Ownership handoff**: `--no-owner` dumps restore as the admin, so the drill hands the database, public schema, and every restored relation to the tenant role (`\gexec`, `%I`-quoted); tenant-role connections prove real access.
- **Provision critical section**: `postgresql.auto.conf` read-modify-write is serialized by a **cluster-wide advisory-lock session** (canonicalized onto the `postgres` database — advisory locks are database-local while the file is cluster-wide), replacing the file-lock protocol entirely.
- **RPO from the manifest**: the manifest inside the encrypted, checksummed archive is authoritative; drifted/future-dated sidecar-manifest pairs fail closed.
- **Linear isolation**: every tenant probed as its own role; ACL assertion covers datdba ownership, PUBLIC-denied, no foreign grantees (OID 0 probe).

# Risks

**None to runtime.** Adds a dev tool + its offline tests under `packages/cloud/scripts/group-room-sim/` and one root `package.json` script (`cloud:group-room-sim`). Nothing imports it. It is a live-model evaluation, not a CI gate; the CI-safe part is the tool's own 41 tests, auto-discovered by the scripts lanes like the existing `admin/hetzner-e2e/` tool.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

A repeatable behavioral evaluation of the five homepage demo rooms (Household, Co-parenting, Friends, Trip, Community) as synthetic multi-party iMessage groups through the real Blooio webhook → gateway → Personal Shared route path against a local cloud stack (`cloud:mock`). One room per run: owner DM `/group`, a pre-link silence probe, `Eliza link CODE`, `Eliza ambient on` where the script calls for unprompted interjections, then the room's human messages in script order with bounded waits at Eliza's scripted beats and bounded silence windows everywhere else.

Scored with assertions a broken or cheating agent cannot pass: silent until linked; replies at the scripted beats; restraint at unscripted points (`UNSOLICITED_MAX`, default 2); no echoed human text (exact / containment / token-Jaccard ≥ 0.8, and echoes earn no fact credit); key-fact recall from the room's own script; zero unsupported-capability claims; speaker awareness. Rooms and the 14 forbidden-claim rules derive from the homepage module at runtime, so the harness cannot drift from the marketing scripts (pinned by a test that re-extracts independently).

Second commit: forbidden-claim hits count only on **first-person capability claims**. The homepage rules are written for marketing copy and on live replies they false-positive on lines where the verb belongs to a human or a list ("If you *send* the address…", "Created: [ ] *Buy* coffee", "set up your personal *workspace*"); a real overclaim still fires ("Want me to check if any of these take reservations?" → booking). `first-person-claims.ts` opens a span at a first-person marker (modals, offers, "let me", "want me to", bare "I" + action verb; negations never open one), closes it at sentence end or subject switch, masks checkbox items and quoted text, and the untouched homepage rules run per span. Over the 125 distinct live replies from tonight's runs: raw hits 27 → 3, all three genuine.

Results from the live runs that motivated #25279, for context (same driver, real Cerebras): unsolicited group replies per room before/after the Stage-1 policy — household 7→1, co-parenting 10→0, friends 10→2, trip 8→2, community 8→1.

## What kind of change is this?

Tests / developer tooling (non-breaking).

# Risks

**Medium.** This changes the browser-side identity and lifecycle of Stripe card-checkout attempts and adds a server-side principal precondition.

The implementation fails closed when durable browser coordination is unavailable. Browsers or embedded WebViews without secure Web Locks, durable localStorage, or secure UUID generation receive actionable guidance instead of starting an uncoordinated checkout.

Ambiguous checkout outcomes deliberately retain their idempotency key. A stale different-amount checkout requires reconciliation instead of silently rotating payment identity.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Replaces per-mount card-checkout UUIDs with one durable, cross-tab intent per organization.
- Serializes intent reservation, session binding, and exact cleanup through Web Locks and compare-and-swap localStorage records.
- Reuses the same key for the same initiating user, organization, and amount; rotates it on principal or submitted-amount changes.
- Treats sessionStorage only as a best-effort success-page pointer and falls back to an exact localStorage namespace scan.
- Pins the UI principal in checkout requests with `expectedUserId` and `expectedOrganizationId`.
- Rejects a changed principal with `409 CHECKOUT_PRINCIPAL_CHANGED` before catalog, order, customer-authority, or Stripe work.
- Invalidates delayed responses synchronously on unmount or principal changes before bind/navigation.
- Disables the amount and card/crypto controls while a checkout request is pending.
- Clears only the exact session after authoritative `success: true` verification.
- Keeps verified payment success visible if non-authoritative browser cleanup fails, with an accessible warning.
- Adds canonical English i18n entries and regression coverage.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking).

## Out of scope

- No Stripe webhook, settlement, refund, database schema, or customer-authority policy change.
- No crypto/direct-wallet checkout behavior change.
- No hardware-checkout contract change.
- No pricing, amount-limit, or amount-step policy change.
- No real Stripe charge was made by the visual evidence harness.

# Documentation changes needed?

My changes do not require project-documentation changes. User-facing English strings were added to the canonical locale.

## Executive Summary
This week, the ElizaOS project focused on hardening the core framework to ensure high reliability and consistent performance across all agent interactions. By standardizing our data handling and refining our cloud infrastructure, we have built a more stable foundation for complex, autonomous multi-agent collaboration.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Strengthening System Reliability and Data Integrity**
_Goal: We aimed to eliminate unpredictable errors and data corruption to ensure our agents behave consistently in every environment._
- Standardized how the system processes text and data, preventing errors caused by incompatible character formats ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/27967), [#28835](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/28835)).
- Implemented strict data checks to ensure calculations remain accurate and predictable ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/25970), [#29949](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/29949)).

**Enhancing Cloud Security and Agent Orchestration**
_Goal: We focused on securing our cloud environment to support safer, more sophisticated interactions between multiple agents._
- Introduced new consent and authentication protocols to ensure secure agent provisioning and group interactions ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/28361), [#29903](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/29903)).
- Optimized cloud performance and reliability, ensuring that agents can handle large tasks and recover quickly from service interruptions ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/29685), [#29695](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/29695)).

**Advancing Autonomous Agent Capabilities**
_Goal: We are expanding the framework's ability to perform complex, real-world tasks through collaborative and adversarial testing._
- Enabled new "agent arenas" where AI can practice autonomous sales negotiations and collaborative problem-solving ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/29533)).
- Improved the tools agents use to interact with computer interfaces, allowing for more precise and reliable coding assistance ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/28389), [#28287](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/28287)).

**Canonicalizing the User Experience**
_Goal: We are simplifying our design system to make the platform easier to maintain and more consistent for our users._
- Unified the layout and design of core application components, such as transcripts and file management, to create a more cohesive experience ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/29598), [#29729](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/29729)).
- Refactored features into modular plugins, which allows for faster loading times and a cleaner, more flexible architecture ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/29151)).

## Goal

Ship the first core Eliza product launch so that a brand-new user can open eliza.app, understand the product, create or sign into an account, get a useful result from Eliza, and bring that same useful agent into real conversations.

The launch bar is the real product journey, not the existence of code paths:

- The eliza.app front door, authentication, and onboarding work without dead ends.
- Eliza provides useful value on the first session and across repeat sessions.
- Native group chat works well in Discord, iMessage, and WhatsApp.
- Telegram and X work as supported first-class channels at minimum.
- Every advertised staging login and launch workflow is repeatably testable end to end.
- Cloudflare, database, control-plane, gateway, and sandbox evidence can explain every failed or successful run.

This is the acceptance and coordination parent. It must be delivered through bounded child issues and PRs, not as one monolithic implementation.

The product priority is the web/core front door. New macOS feature expansion or polish is subordinate until this exit gate is green.

### Shared-bot and runtime routing contract

Every messaging entrypoint in this launch uses an environment-specific **shared provider identity maintained by the Eliza team**. End users do not create or own Discord bots, Telegram bots, phone senders, WhatsApp identities, or X ingress accounts.

The required journey is:

1. an external sender contacts the existing staging or production shared bot/account;
2. if the sender is not linked, that same bot starts onboarding and sends the user to the central Eliza sign-in page;
3. the user may authenticate with any supported login method — the login provider is independent of the messaging channel;
4. successful authentication securely links the external channel identity back to the canonical Eliza account and resumes the original conversation;
5. subsequent messages continue through the same shared provider bot, while backend routing selects either the user-scoped **Personal Shared** runtime or the user's active **Dedicated** agent in its sandbox;
6. upgrading to Dedicated changes the compute target, not the Discord/Telegram/etc. bot identity.

Group bindings preserve the same separation: one team-maintained provider bot and exactly one onboarded owner whose Personal Shared or Dedicated runtime owns the group. Other participants may converse as guests without individual onboarding, but they cannot inherit owner authority, use owner-only tools, or access private user memory.

- Run `review-security` for auth/session/identity changes and `review-bugbot` for every candidate code change before ready-for-review.86:T11ab,## Summary
`defaultSpawn` in plugins/plugin-cli-inference/src/claude-cli.ts (shared by both the Claude and Codex production inference paths via codex-cli-exec.ts) opens the required `/dev/null` stdin file descriptor with `openSync(opts.stdinPath, "r")` and passes the raw fd into `spawn(...)` stdio, but never closes the parent's copy of that fd. Node dups the fd into the child at spawn time; the parent's descriptor stays open forever. Every `ClaudeCli.generate()` / `CodexCli.exec()` call — i.e. every large-tier chat/route/synthesis inference turn when ELIZA_CHAT_VIA_CLI is enabled — leaks exactly one fd. On a long-running agent this monotonically grows the process fd table until it hits the OS limit and subsequent spawns/opens fail with EMFILE, taking down the inference route (and anything else needing an fd). This is the core inference data path, so the leak is unbounded in normal operation, not an edge case.

## Reproduction
```
Mechanism proven with a standalone reproduction that mirrors defaultSpawn's exact stdio handling (openSync + spawn with the fd, detached, no close):
  /tmp/fdtest.mjs: opens /dev/null via openSync, spawns a child with stdio:[fd,'pipe','pipe'], never closes fd; loops 20 times counting /proc/self/fd.
  Observed: "fds before: 21" -> "fds after 20 spawns: 42" (one fd leaked per call).
Control with the fix (closeSync(fd) after spawn), /tmp/fdtest2.mjs and fdtest3.mjs:
  Observed: "fds after 20 spawns (with closeSync): 22" (flat), and child stdin still functions — child reads "EOF:0" from /dev/null, so closing the parent copy immediately after spawn does not break the child's stdin.
Expected per the file's own contract ("`/dev/null` stdin is REQUIRED"): the fd is a per-call resource that must be released; observed: it is never closed, so N inference calls hold N open fds.
```

## Proposed fix
In defaultSpawn (plugins/plugin-cli-inference/src/claude-cli.ts), close the parent's copy of stdinFd once the child has inherited it. Since libuv dups the fd synchronously during spawn, add `try { closeSync(stdinFd); } catch {}` immediately after the `spawn(...)` call returns (import closeSync from node:fs). This releases the descriptor for both the success and error/timeout paths without touching the child's stdin (verified: child still sees /dev/null EOF). Scope is ~2 lines plus the import; both CLI variants share this spawner so a single fix covers claude-cli and codex-cli-exec. Test plan (>=10 real lines) added to __tests__/cli-inference.test.ts alongside the existing real-spawn "defaultSpawn timeout escalation" block: a test that snapshots readdirSync('/proc/self/fd').length, runs defaultSpawn against a trivial real child (process.execPath -e 'process.exit(0)') ~15 times with stdinPath '/dev/null', and asserts the post-run fd count has not grown by more than a small constant (proving no per-call leak). Gate the assertion on process.platform === 'linux' (procfs) or use a portable fd probe; the existing suite already spawns real children here so no new harness is required.

## Evidence plan
The PR will attach: (1) the new failing-before/passing-after fd-count test output from `bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-cli-inference test`; (2) a before/after /proc/self/fd count from a loop of real defaultSpawn calls showing linear growth pre-fix and flat post-fix; (3) confirmation the child stdin still receives EOF from /dev/null after the immediate close (child prints EOF marker), proving the fix does not regress the "stdin REQUIRED" behavior the file documents.

8c:T1977,## Summary
The route-level model downloader `downloadModel` in `plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/local-inference-routes.ts` resumes an interrupted download by sending a `Range: bytes=<n>-` header and then opening the staging file in append mode whenever a `.part` file exists (`flags: existingPartial > 0 ? "a" : "w"`). It never verifies the server actually honored the range (HTTP 206). If the origin ignores Range and replies HTTP 200 with the full body — common for CDN redirect targets, gated/proxy repos, or mirrors — the full file is appended onto the stale partial bytes, producing a corrupt GGUF. `record.total` is also miscomputed as `existingPartial + fullSize`. The corruption passes the only integrity check (`isGgufFile` reads just the first 4 bytes, which are still "GGUF" from the old partial), and there is no sha256 verification against an expected hash, so the corrupt file is renamed to final, registered as an installed model, and auto-assigned to the TEXT_SMALL/TEXT_LARGE/TEXT_EMBEDDING slots via `ensureDefaultAssignment`. The sibling canonical `services/downloader.ts` in the same package already guards this exact case (`if (startByte > 0 && response.statusCode !== 206) { startByte = 0; received = 0 }` then `flags: startByte > 0 ? "a" : "w"`); the route-level copy diverged and dropped the guard.

## Reproduction
```
Ran a local Vitest probe in plugins/plugin-local-inference (real fs + real local HTTP origin; only ELIZA_STATE_DIR and ELIZA_HF_BASE_URL redirected). Steps: (1) set ELIZA_HF_BASE_URL to a local http server that IGNORES Range and always answers `200` with the full body `GGUF`+`REAL-MODEL-BODY` (19 bytes); (2) seed a stale partial `<state>/local-inference/downloads/eliza-1-2b.part` = `GGUF`+`STALE-PARTIAL`; (3) call the exported `applyLocalInferenceManagementMutation({ op: "start_download", modelId: "eliza-1-2b" })`, which runs `startDownload` -> `downloadModel`; (4) poll for the final file `<state>/local-inference/models/eliza-1-2b.gguf`.
Observed output: `stored length: 36 expected: 19` and `stored bytes: "GGUFSTALE-PARTIALGGUFREAL-MODEL-BODY"`. Expected: exactly `GGUFREAL-MODEL-BODY` (19 bytes). The corrupt file was renamed to final and written into registry.json as an installed model. Test asserted `stored.equals(FULL)` -> failed (false). Command: `npx vitest run src/__probe_resume.test.ts`.
```

## Proposed fix
Mirror the sibling downloader's guard in `downloadModel`: after receiving the response and validating 2xx, compute `let effectiveStart = existingPartial; if (existingPartial > 0 && response.statusCode !== 206) { effectiveStart = 0; record.received = 0; }`, then use `effectiveStart` for both `record.total = effectiveStart + contentLength` and `flags: effectiveStart > 0 ? "a" : "w"`. Bounded to ~6 lines in one function; no signature/API change. Test plan (>=10 lines, honest): a Vitest suite standing up two local http origins — one that honors Range (206 + remaining bytes) and one that ignores it (200 + full body) — seeding a stale `.part`, driving `applyLocalInferenceManagementMutation({op:"start_download"})`, and asserting the final `models/<id>.gguf` bytes exactly equal the full file in BOTH cases (correct resume for 206, clean restart for 200); plus a regression assertion that `record.total`/registry size match the true file length. The probe already written proves the failing case and converts directly into the 200-path test.

## Evidence plan
The PR will attach: the failing-before / passing-after Vitest output for both the 200 (ignore-range) and 206 (honor-range) origins; a hexdump/length comparison of the stored `models/<id>.gguf` showing 19 bytes (correct) vs the current 36-byte `GGUFSTALE-PARTIALGGUFREAL-MODEL-BODY` corruption; and a diff showing the route-level guard now matches services/downloader.ts (statusCode !== 206 -> restart from 0).

<!-- eliza-computer-attribution:v1 {"provider":"openai","model":"gpt-5.6-sol","client":"Codex Desktop / multi-agent","skill_revision":"N/A - no repository contribution skill used"} -->8e:T107b,## Summary
`defaultSpawn` in claude-cli.ts is the production spawner for BOTH the Claude and Codex CLI inference variants (codex-cli-exec.ts routes through the same seam). On every call it does `stdinFd = openSync(opts.stdinPath, "r")` (opts.stdinPath is always "/dev/null") and hands that raw fd to `spawn(..., { stdio: [stdinFd, "pipe", "pipe"] })`, but never closes it. Node/libuv dups the fd for the child during spawn; the parent's copy is leaked. There is no closeSync anywhere in the file. Each ClaudeCli.generate()/CodexCli.generate() call — i.e. every inference turn served over the SAFE/CLI route — leaks exactly one file descriptor in the host process. Under sustained agent use this monotonically climbs to the process fd limit and then every subsequent openSync/socket/file operation fails with EMFILE, taking down inference and anything else in the runtime that needs a descriptor. This is a slow-burn resource leak on the hottest path of the plugin, not a cold error branch.

## Reproduction
```
Node's stdio-fd sharing does not close the parent fd. Reproduced the exact pattern used by defaultSpawn:

/tmp/fdleak.mjs (openSync("/dev/null","r") + spawn(stdio:[fd,"pipe","pipe"], detached:true), no close, 50 iterations, counting /proc/self/fd):
  $ node fdleak.mjs
  fds before: 21 after 50 spawns: 72 delta: 51
=> ~1 leaked fd per spawn (50 spawns → +51 open descriptors).

Adding `closeSync(stdinFd)` in the child 'close'/'error' handlers (the proposed fix):
  $ node fdfix.mjs
  fds before: 21 after 50: 22 delta: 1
=> leak eliminated. Confirms both the defect and the fix.
```

## Proposed fix
In defaultSpawn (claude-cli.ts), close the parent's copy of stdinFd once it has been handed to the child. Minimal change: define `const closeStdin = () => { try { closeSync(stdinFd); } catch {} };` (import closeSync from node:fs) and call it in both terminal handlers — `child.on("error", (err) => { clearTimers(); closeStdin(); reject(err); })` and `child.on("close", (code, signal) => { clearTimers(); closeStdin(); resolve(...) })`. Also guard the case where `spawn()` throws synchronously by wrapping it so stdinFd is closed on that path too. libuv dups the fd during spawn, so closing after the child is created is safe and does not affect the child's stdin. Test plan (Linux-gated vitest, ~15 lines, real defaultSpawn, no spawn mock): resolve a trivial binary, snapshot readdirSync('/proc/self/fd').length, invoke defaultSpawn 30+ times awaiting each, snapshot again, assert the delta is small (< 5) rather than ≈ call count; a second assertion runs the pre-fix pattern inline to document the ≈1-per-call growth the fix removes.

## Evidence plan
PR attaches: (1) before/after `node` fd-count reproduction output shown above (delta 51 → delta 1); (2) the new Linux-gated vitest failing on the current code (fd delta ≈ call count) and passing after the closeSync fix; (3) `bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-cli-inference test` and typecheck output green.

## Independent deep review: #29921 — same-provider cutover/recovery certification

Source `b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f`; live issue/comments and current routing, bridge, import and identity consumers reviewed. This adds a concrete recovery failure to the qualification matrix. No connector message, account linking, billing, provisioning or live transition was performed.

### P1 — Failed nonempty history restoration is replaced by an empty import and returned as success (reproduced)

On `Bridge returned HTTP 404`, [deliverPersonalTextMessage](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/personal-message-delivery.ts#L130-L177) fetches Shared history and tries to import it. If a nonempty full import returns no receipt—or some historical messages lack source IDs—it calls `importCanonicalConversation` again with an **empty array**. A successful empty receipt permits retrying the message; an ordinary reply then returns `success:true`. The [personal-shared connector route](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/cloud/api/internal/eliza-app/personal-shared/messages/route.ts#L1788-L1841) duplicates this behavior for its maintained ingress paths and group-specific room.

Executed `bun /tmp/guardian-project19-deep-review/probe-29921.ts` against the source-extracted unchanged complete delivery helper, with controlled bridge/history/import collaborators:

| Input state | Observed operations | Final result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One historical message; full import rejects | bridge404 → import(1) fails → import(0) succeeds → bridge retry | `success:true` |
| Two historical messages, one lacks ID | bridge404 → import(0) succeeds → bridge retry | `success:true` |
| Genuinely empty source history | bridge404 → import(0) → bridge retry | `success:true` — valid control |
| Complete nonempty history | bridge404 → import(1) succeeds → bridge retry | `success:true` — valid control |

The probe proves success can bypass the caller's original nonempty restoration requirement. It does not prove data was deleted, a real remote import failed, or a provider received a reply.

Crucial counterevidence: the [importer](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/eliza-sandbox.ts#L6970-L7033) correctly validates inserted+skipped and modern/legacy receipts against the **supplied** message count. Its empty receipt is truthful for zero submitted messages. The caller silently changed the expected source set; adding another `complete:true` check there would not fix this defect. The [agent import endpoint](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/agent/src/api/conversation-routes.ts#L3473-L3530) supports canonical import, so a legitimate empty new session must remain possible.

### Required plan amendment

1. Resolve a typed repair decision distinguishing a genuinely new/empty conversation from required-history restoration. Capture immutable expected source IDs/count and provenance before import. Preserve the entire selected history; missing IDs require an explicit migration/reconciliation outcome, not omission or fabricated IDs without a migration contract.
2. Remove empty fallback when a nonempty source requires restoration. Return a typed recoverable unavailable/incomplete state and keep the same input message identity pending. A failure may have partially imported data, so retry the same canonical import idempotently and reconcile actual receipt/state instead of creating another conversation.
3. Consolidate the duplicated repair policy into the canonical delivery/import seam while retaining provider/group identity and the existing private-vs-group room separation. The generic helper is currently called by the X personal-DM route; it is not evidence that all providers already share this entire implementation. The other connector route needs the same repair.
4. Bind completion evidence to the original required source set and target conversation, not only the latest import call's count. For #25146 recovery, substitute the explicitly authorized fallback interval and generation; do not select the old pre-upgrade archive or permit Dedicated-to-Shared import.
5. Add actual DB+agent import tests for full import rejection, partial import then retry, mixed/missing source IDs, process restart after import-before-message retry, and a genuinely empty new conversation. Preserve same input message ID on retry and prove the resulting model request includes every required historical message exactly once before substantive generation. Then run the authorized same-provider journey with a distinctive prior fact; receipt/readback and the complete model context must agree.

90:Te5e,## Problem

Production Telegram turns on 2026-08-28 stopped producing a visible response after successful earlier exchanges. This is a second failure mode beside the split bot identity in #29763.

The Personal Shared internal route correctly maps SharedRuntimeCacheWarmingError to retryable HTTP 503 with Retry-After and safe X-Eliza-Failure-* headers. Later failures inside AgentRuntime are wrapped as a generic Error by run-shared-agent-turn.ts. The route therefore emits a generic 500, the direct Telegram edge retries a bounded number of times, then throws Personal Shared edge turn failed (<status>). The final provider turn receives no reply or safe fallback, and the underlying runtime/action/provider classification is lost.

The screenshots include a reminder delete request immediately before one silent interval. The existing Reminder parity issue #29688 owns the mutation behavior itself. This issue owns transport/runtime classification and the guarantee that a Telegram DM cannot end silently after an acknowledged inbound update.

## Confirmed evidence

- Four correlated production Telegram edge turns were inspected without publishing chat/user IDs or message bodies.
- The first failing class was retryable SharedRuntimeCacheWarmingError / 503.
- Later turns ended as generic AgentRuntime turn failed / 500 after bounded retries.
- The outer Worker log did not retain the safe inner cause class, so the exact downstream action/provider cause cannot be proven from current telemetry.
- Concurrent invalid API-key traffic had no trace/request intersection with the Telegram turns and is not causal.
- Railway logs in the screenshot window do not own these Telegram failures; the direct Cloudflare edge does.

## Scope

- Introduce a dependency-light, cause-preserving Shared runtime turn error with an allowlisted safe failure class and retry disposition.
- Preserve safe stage/name/retry metadata through the internal Personal Shared response, direct Telegram edge, and Railway gateway handoff without exposing provider payloads, prompts, SQL, credentials, or user content.
- Keep cache warming and transient provider/runtime availability failures retryable with bounded Retry-After semantics.
- Keep invariant/action-contract failures terminal and visible; do not replay a non-idempotent mutation after an ambiguous provider side effect.
- After retries are exhausted, deliver one truthful, non-duplicating Telegram fallback when egress is still safe, or persist a recoverable delivery state that allows a provider retry.
- Add behavioral tests for warming, transient provider failure, terminal action-contract failure, exhausted retry, exact-once fallback, and safe log/header redaction.
- Relate Reminder failures to #29688 without duplicating its parser/mutation implementation.
- No merge, deployment, live message, secret/config mutation, provider action, or webhook change is authorized here.

## Acceptance

- A safe underlying failure class and retry disposition survive AgentRuntime wrapping and both transport boundaries.
- Retryable failures remain retryable; terminal failures are not blindly replayed.
- Every accepted private Telegram update ends in exactly one of: durable normal reply, durable truthful fallback, explicit provider retry state, or a classified delivery receipt visible to operators.
- No final generic Personal Shared edge turn failed error is the only evidence available.
- Focused Shared runtime, Worker edge, gateway, and exact-once tests pass.
- A later separately authorized production/staging probe proves a normal reply and an injected safe failure path without duplicate egress.

98:T1495,## Summary
`defaultSpawn` in plugins/plugin-cli-inference/src/claude-cli.ts opens `/dev/null` with `openSync(opts.stdinPath, "r")` (line 94) and passes the numeric fd to `spawn` as `stdio[0]` (line 105), but never closes the PARENT process's copy of that descriptor. When a raw integer fd is handed to child_process stdio, Node/Bun does not close the parent's fd — the caller owns it. So every `ClaudeCli.generate()` / `CodexCli.generate()` call (the cold `claude`/`codex` CLI inference backends, both routed through this single `defaultSpawn`) leaks exactly one open descriptor for the lifetime of the agent process. A long-running agent doing repeated CLI-route inference monotonically accumulates open fds until it hits the process `ulimit -n`, after which every subsequent `openSync`/`spawn` (and other I/O across the whole process) fails with EMFILE — breaking not just inference but all file/socket operations. This is a teardown/resource-lifecycle defect on a real production path, not input validation.

## Reproduction
```
The leak is in claude-cli.ts lines 88-106: `stdinFd = openSync(opts.stdinPath, "r")`, then `spawn(argv[0], argv.slice(1), { stdio: [stdinFd, "pipe", "pipe"], detached: true })`, and `stdinFd` is never closed in `child.on("close")`/`"error"`/anywhere (grep confirms: the only `openSync`/`stdinFd` references are lines 2,90,94,105; no `closeSync` exists in the package). Faithful minimal repro of those exact lines (Linux, /proc fd count):
  cat > /tmp/fdtest.mjs <<'EOF'
  import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
  import { openSync, readdirSync } from "node:fs";
  const run = () => new Promise((res,rej)=>{ const fd=openSync("/dev/null","r"); const c=spawn("true",[],{stdio:[fd,"pipe","pipe"],detached:true}); c.on("error",rej); c.on("close",()=>res()); });
  const before = readdirSync(`/proc/${process.pid}/fd`).length;
  for (let i=0;i<50;i++) await run();
  await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,200));
  console.log("delta", readdirSync(`/proc/${process.pid}/fd`).length - before);
  EOF
  node /tmp/fdtest.mjs
Observed: `open fds before: 21 after 50 spawns: 72 delta: 51` (one leaked fd per call). Expected: bounded fd count (~0 delta). Adding `child.on("spawn", () => closeSync(fd))` (plus close on error/close) yields `delta 1`, and a `cat` child with the same closed-in-parent /dev/null stdin still exits code 0 at EOF (stdin inheritance intact).
```

## Proposed fix
In `defaultSpawn` (claude-cli.ts), close the parent's copy of `stdinFd` once the child has inherited it. Import `closeSync` from node:fs; add an idempotent `closeStdin()` guard that calls `closeSync(stdinFd)` and invoke it on the child's `"spawn"` event and again (guarded) in the existing `child.on("error")` and `child.on("close")` handlers, plus in the `openSync`-succeeded-but-`spawn`-threw path. This is ~8 changed lines, fully local to one function; the codex variant needs no change because it shares this spawner. Test plan (new src/__tests__/default-spawn-fd.test.ts, >=10 lines of real assertions): (1) capture `readdirSync('/proc/'+process.pid+'/fd').length`, call the exported `defaultSpawn(['true'], {cwd: tmpdir, env: {}, timeoutMs: 5000, stdinPath: '/dev/null'})` (or `[process.execPath, '-e', '']`) 40 times awaiting each, then assert the post delta is small/bounded (e.g. < 5) — this fails on current develop (delta ~40) and passes after the fix; (2) assert a `defaultSpawn` run whose child reads stdin still receives EOF (resolves, non-hanging) so the close does not break stdin inheritance; (3) assert the returned SpawnResult still has code 0. Guarded on `process.platform === 'linux'` for the /proc probe (repo CI is Linux) with a closeSync spy fallback assertion for portability.

## Evidence plan
The PR will attach: (a) the failing-then-passing test output for the new fd-leak test (before-fix delta vs after-fix bounded delta); (b) a raw `/proc/self/fd` count before/after 50 real `defaultSpawn` invocations on current develop vs patched, demonstrating leak (delta ~51 → ~1); (c) the stdin-inheritance sanity run showing a child still reads /dev/null EOF and exits 0 after the parent fd is closed; (d) `bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-cli-inference test` and typecheck/lint green.

In the browser fallback CameraWeb (plugins/plugin-native-camera/src/web.ts), startRecording() opens a separate microphone stream via getUserMedia({audio:true}) and merges its audio tracks into a new MediaStream used for the MediaRecorder. Those audio tracks are never stopped: stopRecording() only stops the MediaRecorder and builds the blob, and stopPreview() only stops this.mediaStream (which holds the video tracks). The audio MediaStream reference is local to startRecording and lost after it returns, so the microphone hardware stays active indefinitely after recording ends — the OS mic indicator remains lit (a privacy leak), and each subsequent startRecording opens and leaks another microphone track. This violates the resource-teardown contract the rest of the class follows for the video stream.

## Reproduction
```
Probe test added to plugins/plugin-native-camera/src (jsdom env), mocking navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia (returns a video track for the video request and a distinct audio track for the {audio:true} request), MediaRecorder, MediaStream, and firing the internal <video> onloadedmetadata so stopRecording resolves. Sequence: new CameraWeb(); startPreview({element}); startRecording({audio:true}); stopRecording(); stopPreview(); then expect(audioTrack.stop).toHaveBeenCalled().
Command: cd plugins/plugin-native-camera && node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/leak.probe.test.ts
Observed: FAIL — "expected vi.fn() to be called at least once"; the audio track's stop() is never invoked. Expected: after teardown the microphone track is stopped. (Confirmed by code: no getAudioTracks()/audioStream.stop path exists anywhere in web.ts.)
```

## Proposed fix
Persist the microphone stream (or its audio tracks) on a private field when startRecording opens it, and stop those tracks in stopRecording()'s onstop handler (and defensively in stopPreview) after the blob is assembled — mirroring the existing this.mediaStream.getTracks().forEach(track => track.stop()) teardown. Keep the recorder's merged stream but ensure the extra audio tracks are torn down exactly once. Test plan (>=10 lines): a jsdom vitest spec asserting (1) the audio track stop() is called after stopRecording, (2) it is not called before, (3) a second startRecording/stopRecording cycle stops the newly-opened audio track, and (4) stopPreview during an active recording also stops audio tracks. Harness mocks getUserMedia/MediaRecorder/MediaStream as in the probe.

## Evidence plan
The PR attaches the failing-before/passing-after vitest run for the new spec plus the existing web.test.ts suite, and a short note showing the code path (startRecording audio getUserMedia vs. stopPreview only stopping this.mediaStream video tracks) that proves the leak is on the real user recording path.
