## Product contract — revised for Sprint 3

When confirmed server-side billing/entitlement policy withdraws Dedicated access, the user may continue eligible free operations on Personal Shared. **Shared must have no access to Dedicated memory during fallback.** This requirement supersedes the former import-before-fallback design. Preserve Dedicated data for entitled recovery; do not copy, retrieve, summarize, embed, or include it in Shared prompts or fallback context. A shared schema or database does not grant cross-tier data access.

Shared receives a typed, minimal account provider: access state, confirmed reason category, safe deadline if applicable, available free capabilities, and an authorized sign-in/billing recovery action. Say plainly that Dedicated memory is unavailable until billing is restored. Do not expose card details, raw Stripe objects, secrets, or unrelated account data. Keep normal free Calendar/Notes and other eligible capability state separate from protected Dedicated memory; restoration of a schema pointer must not bypass that boundary.

## Existing architecture and remaining gap

The current personal target resolver deliberately retains Dedicated authority through sleep/error/restart and completed cutover markers, without a billing-loss state machine. Reuse the canonical identity, route, entitlement and durable command authorities; do not add another gateway router or billing scheduler. Dependencies: #30638, #23091, #23093, #23094, #23095, #23096, #23098; same-bot certification #29921 and ingress/group contracts #29919/#29920.

## Required behavior

- One typed durable transition owner with revision/generation fencing: dedicated_active → fallback_pending → shared_active → recovery_pending → dedicated_active, plus explicit waiting/failed/unavailable outcomes. Confirm current account/tenant/owner entitlement at every effect and final route commit.
- Distinguish confirmed nonpayment/expired access from low credit, trial expiration, grace/dunning, canceled-at-period-end, provider outage, webhook lag, sleeping/starting Dedicated and unknown billing state. Product policy must define which condition withdraws entitlement; never equate every transient error or zero incidental cash balance to subscription loss.
- Finish, cancel or honestly fail in-flight work under one request owner. Route new requests to one active destination; retries and stale workers cannot generate duplicate replies, writes, charges or instance starts.
- Before Shared activation, establish a separate scoped fallback conversation/journal and revoke Shared access to Dedicated context. There is **no Dedicated-to-Shared memory import step**. Pre-upgrade archives or cached provider context cannot be used to reconstruct protected Dedicated history.
- Persist the Shared interval completely and with provenance. After confirmed payment/entitlement recovery, Dedicated may idempotently reconcile that explicitly scoped interval, verify health/current authority and then own routing again. Maintain data lineage and user-visible continuity without exposing Dedicated data while access is suspended.
- Recovery links are signed/expiring and require appropriate interactive identity and role at use. They return the user to the original authorized conversation after successful billing reconciliation; a checkout redirect alone cannot restore access.
- Dedupe transition, warning/deadline, payment-action and recovery notifications by durable generation. Billing/system notices remain deliverable without a paid workflow subscription.

## Acceptance and edge cases

- A confirmed expired/unpaid account falls to Shared, receives conversational account-aware recovery help, and can perform eligible free operations. Asking Shared about Dedicated-only prior work yields accurate unavailable state and zero Dedicated retrieval.
- Subscription active but usage/media allowance exhausted is not mislabeled unpaid. Canceled-at-period-end retains entitled access until the approved boundary. Trial, grace, late invoice, revoked account, refund/dispute and provider-unknown policies are explicit.
- Two paid users on one gateway each route to their own Dedicated, never Shared or the other user's instance. Mixed Shared/Dedicated users, linked connectors, owner-bound groups, unlink/relink, owner changes and stale routing caches preserve authority and reply destination.
- Payment success/replay/reordered webhook, failure during provisioning, crash before/after route commit, suspended/failed instance, repeated recovery, cancellation during recovery and deletion all converge without duplicate effects or premature memory access.
- Memory/state references retain complete values; no lossy compaction or implicit recent window. A failed reconciliation is an explicit recoverable state, not fabricated success.

## Verification

Real PostgreSQL/PGlite transition, restart and concurrency contracts; real signed Stripe sandbox lifecycle; dedicated instance health/route readback; actual ingress/egress receipts; live-model fallback and recovered trajectories; controlled account fixtures proving memory remains unavailable throughout fallback. Include desktop/mobile recordings and inspected canonical evidence. Fixtures/mocks alone do not prove live connector routing. Keep private fixture data out of public evidence. No production payment/resource change or live connector message was performed in planning.

## Sprint 3 scope allocation

Project: https://github.com/orgs/elizaOS/projects/19 . Shaw lead; high complexity; **6 person-days nominal, 5–8 estimated**. Candidate in October 3–16 scope, not a deadline commitment; full Sprint 3 is over capacity. Product decisions on grace, retention, resource funding and recovery are prerequisites, not values inferred here. This replaces the incompatible old fallback-memory acceptance; historical issue revisions remain available.


Project 19 Sprint 3 (October 3–16, 2026): scope candidate, not a capacity-committed completion date. Planning estimate: **6 person-days** for this slice. Preserve existing ownership; @lalalune is the sprint integration lead. Full scope exceeds two-person sprint capacity; sequencing and remaining policy decisions are in the project README.

## Critical implementation audit — 2026-09-06

Source: `8fea4f94c29c7712ce3caf303e3350150622d048`. Source/live issue research only; no account, message, billing, infrastructure or data migration operation occurred.

### Existing routing and incompatible historical assumptions

[Personal target resolution](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/8fea4f94c29c7712ce3caf303e3350150622d048/packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/agent-tier-upgrade-target.ts#L1292) retains a completed server-owned Dedicated cutover through sleep/error/restart. That prevents split histories; it is not an entitlement-driven fallback state machine. [Preparation](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/8fea4f94c29c7712ce3caf303e3350150622d048/packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/personal-dedicated-delivery.ts#L57) returns ready for running, checks the legacy credit gate before idempotent sleep/stop recovery, and otherwise returns explicit blocked/starting/unavailable. The [connector route](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/8fea4f94c29c7712ce3caf303e3350150622d048/packages/cloud/api/internal/eliza-app/personal-shared/messages/route.ts#L1700) returns 402/503 for those outcomes rather than activating Shared. [Personal text delivery](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/8fea4f94c29c7712ce3caf303e3350150622d048/packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/personal-message-delivery.ts#L55) is another consumer of the same target/preparation seam. Both must adopt one authority decision.

[Existing cutover coordination](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/8fea4f94c29c7712ce3caf303e3350150622d048/packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/shared-runtime/conversation-coordinator.ts#L459) can seal Shared admission, wait for an in-flight turn, snapshot and commit/release an exact lease. This is useful concurrency infrastructure, but simply reopening the original Shared identity/archive would violate the revised memory boundary. The historical comment claiming “Shared history reconciliation” is not acceptance of import-on-fallback: **Dedicated → Shared transfer is forbidden during fallback**, including pre-upgrade history that belongs to the protected Dedicated context. Only the newly scoped Shared interval can move in the recovery direction.

### Detailed implementation plan

1. Define provider-neutral eligibility from #30638/#23093/#23094 with account/owner, current entitlement revision, decision reason and availability. Product owners define trial/grace/dunning/access/retention boundaries; #22930 owns reversal/refund/hold restoration. Low cash, active subscription allowance exhaustion, sleeping compute, provider outage and unknown webhook state are not confirmed entitlement withdrawal. Preserve the existing Dedicated route on unknown/transient states with honest unavailability.
2. Extend the canonical durable routing/cutover authority with a revision-fenced transition generation and explicit pending/active/recovering/failed outcomes. Use the existing command/lifecycle/queue owners; no new gateway router, billing poller or competing scheduler. Serialize requests against one active destination. Recheck account ownership, deletion state and entitlement at every external effect and final route CAS.
3. On confirmed withdrawal, drain/cancel/honestly fail the current request under one delivery owner and establish a **new scoped fallback journal/context identity** before admitting Shared. Deny Shared reads from Dedicated stores, pre-upgrade archives, restored pointers and cached providers. Keep eligible free calendar/notes records accessible through their own authorized domain contract, not by importing Dedicated memory. This is an enforced repository/provider access boundary, not just a prompt instruction.
4. Add the minimal account-state provider with typed access/reason/deadline/free-capabilities and authorized recovery action; omit private payment/provider details. Produce a plain truthful memory-unavailable reply when asked about protected Dedicated history. Bind recovery continuation to interactive account authorization and original conversation; use private continuation for group account recovery. Dedupe warning/deadline/action notices by durable transition generation; notices must remain deliverable without a paid workflow entitlement.
5. Recover only after authoritative paid/trial entitlement restoration and Dedicated health. Seal the **fallback interval only**, import/reconcile complete interval data with provenance and idempotent receipts, then commit routing back to the same authorized Dedicated. A successful checkout redirect is insufficient. Crash/retry at each stage must resume the same command/instance; failed reconciliation remains explicit and must not expose Dedicated memory through Shared. Never summarize, compact or silently omit history.
6. Extend target/delivery/coordinator tests and real DB concurrent transition/restart coverage: repeated withdrawal/recovery, entitlement changes during import, stale workers/cache, webhook reorder, in-flight late replies, account deletion, owner/link changes and two users sharing one gateway identity. Use distinct marker data to prove zero Dedicated retrieval while fallback is active and complete eligible Shared interval recovery afterward.
7. Under #29921/#25076's existing live gates, run signed sandbox billing transitions with actual Dedicated health/route readback and provider ingress/egress receipts. Inspect Shared and recovered live-model requests plus authorized DB artifacts, desktop/mobile recordings and the verified evidence bundle. Run affected shared/API/core tests/typecheck/lint/root verify, app audit for UI changes, and independent security review of the memory/tenant boundary. Public evidence excludes private fixture content.

Scope/capacity: six nominal days (5–8) cover this new reversible authority and isolated-memory workflow only once generic billing, policy and renewable fixture dependencies are ready. Existing upgrade helpers do not eliminate the need for new transition and access proofs. #29919/#29920 own ingress/group semantics; #29921 certifies integrated routing; do not absorb their epics. A search for PRs mentioning #25146 found none, which is not proof no active implementation owner exists—coordinate with the existing claimant before writing.

## Independent deep review: #25146

Revision `b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f`. Reviewed live revised contract, target authority, delivery preparation and both consumers, Personal Shared identity, runtime execution, REST history and cutover coordination. The reversible entitlement workflow remains missing; the deeper findings below identify specific integration constraints rather than claiming an existing fallback was exercised.

### P1 implementation constraint — Isolate the fallback journal without inventing a new account authority

The proposed “new scoped fallback journal/context identity” needs two distinct identities. [Personal Shared authority](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/shared-runtime/personal-shared-identity.ts#L10-L41) derives the exact agent ID from organization+user and verifies equality. [Runtime execution](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/shared-runtime/shared-runtime-chat.ts#L580-L624) grants the authenticated personal-user flag and personal media/reminder ports only for canonical identity plus platform funding. Appending a fallback generation to `agent.id` to obtain a clean history would fail that authority check and also change todo/reminder scopes. Conversely, retaining both old agent and old room reopens the old journal the revised product contract prohibits.

Keep canonical account authority stable and introduce a separately authorized fallback **conversation/journal generation**, resolved server-side from the entitlement transition. [Coordinator addressing](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/shared-runtime/conversation-coordinator.ts#L222-L228) already accepts independent agent/room keys; use this seam deliberately. Current [personal text delivery](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/personal-message-delivery.ts#L53-L59) and its Shared branch pass the canonical agent ID as room. Update all ingress, REST history, model/cache, reminder provenance and recovery consumers through one typed active-journal mapping. The current REST conversation list/create/update still derive a single conversation from agent identity; changing only the connector writer leaves clients reading a different history.

Acceptance: same authenticated account/free capabilities across fallback, a distinct empty authorized fallback journal at activation, and no old-journal data in the actual model/provider request. Repeated fallback generations cannot reuse an earlier suspended interval inadvertently. Separately prove permitted free domain records survive; isolating conversation history must not silently erase todos/calendar capability state.

### P1 implementation constraint — Readiness is not current entitlement or an effect authorization fence

[preparePersonalDedicatedDelivery](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/personal-dedicated-delivery.ts#L57-L131) returns ready immediately for `running`. Sleeping/stopped checks legacy credit, awaits worker health, and queues a wake/resume with account IDs but no entitlement revision. Executed the unchanged source-extracted helper in `/tmp/guardian-project19-deep-review/probe-25146.ts`: running produced ready with zero gate calls; a controlled entitlement-state change during the health await still reached enqueue. This proves helper control flow, **not** actual unauthorized compute: the controlled entitlement variable is an external scenario marker, and downstream workers may impose additional policy.

The new transition cannot be installed only inside the sleeping branch or only in billing webhooks. Produce an authoritative typed entitlement/route decision before both running and sleeping delivery; fence lifecycle jobs and final route commit with its revision, and revalidate after awaited work. Unknown billing/worker state must preserve explicit unavailability, not trigger fallback. Run actual worker/DB races with withdrawal during health check, provisioning, interval import and final commit. Assert stale jobs cannot reactivate routing or create additional instances after a newer generation wins.

### P2 integration constraint — Repair imports need the active interval, not the historic canonical room

Both Dedicated delivery consumers contain a bridge-404 recovery import from `coordinateSharedHistory(agent.id, originalConversationId)`. The deeper #29921 review identifies their empty-import fallback after a failed full import. Even after repairing that completeness defect, this old-room repair path cannot be reused for entitlement recovery without an authorized interval selection. It would select the pre-upgrade journal instead of the newly scoped fallback interval. Reconciliation must carry journal generation, source interval bounds/provenance, complete source count/digest and a receipt bound to the target and transition. Reuse actual import machinery, not its old identity assumptions; do not transfer any Dedicated history into Shared.

### Existing protections to preserve and precise remaining proof

[Target selection](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/agent-tier-upgrade-target.ts#L1299-L1367) checks account/organization ownership, server-owned cutover authority/version and quarantines unverified markers. It deliberately retains Dedicated authority through sleep/error. The cutover coordinator serializes admission and seals an exact snapshot under a token. These are real protections; removing authority or releasing an old seal merely to route Shared is not an acceptable shortcut.

No observed production entitlement withdrawal, memory leak, billing provider run, DB transition or infrastructure mutation is claimed. The missing workflow's acceptance requires actual read-boundary isolation and revision-fenced effects, not a prompt that says memory is unavailable. Extend the first plan with the identity/journal split, all-consumer mapping and current-entitlement fences above before estimating implementation closure. Bun helper probe passed; full DB/runtime tests require the established authorized fixtures and were not run.

- Exact commands and outcomes for focused tests, builds, audits, and known repository-wide baseline blockers.9f:T156f,## Summary
SwabbleWeb.start() (Web Speech fallback in plugins/plugin-native-swabble/src/web.ts) assigns this.recognition, then `await`s startAudioLevelMonitoring() (which itself awaits getUserMedia) BEFORE calling recognition.start(). getUserMedia is always asynchronous, so any stop() that runs during that await interleaves: stop() sets isActive=false, calls this.recognition.stop() (a no-op, recognition not started yet), sets this.recognition=null, and calls stopAudioLevelMonitoring() while the level-meter stream/interval do not yet exist. When start() then resumes it creates this.mediaStream + a 100ms setInterval and calls recognition.start(), whose onstart sets isActive=true and re-emits state "listening". The net result after a start()+stop() sequence: the microphone MediaStream stays live (browser mic indicator on — privacy leak), the audioLevel interval fires forever, and the SpeechRecognition instance keeps running and auto-restarting via onend (isActive===true) — yet this.recognition is null, so no later stop() can ever free it. isListening() reports {listening:true} after the consumer already called stop(). This is a state-machine/teardown-survival race distinct from the fatal-recognition-error leak fixed by merged PR #22656 (that fix only tears down on onerror/onend, neither of which fires here).

## Reproduction
```
In plugins/plugin-native-swabble (node_modules present) I added a probe vitest reusing the file's FakeRecognition harness plus minimal AudioContext/analyser mocks and a getUserMedia returning a deferred promise wrapping a stream whose track.stop() is spied. Sequence: const p = plugin.start({config:{triggers:["eliza"]}}); await Promise.resolve(); await plugin.stop(); resolveGum(stream); await p. Then assert plugin.isListening() === {listening:false}, FakeRecognition.latest.running === false, and track.stopped === true. Observed via `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/probe-race.test.ts`: `AssertionError: expected { listening: true } to deeply equal { listening: false }` — the plugin remains listening with recognition.running true and the mic track never stopped, after the consumer already called stop(). Expected: a start()+stop() sequence must leave the plugin fully torn down (not listening, recognition stopped, mic released). Probe file removed after the run; `git status --short plugins/` is clean.
```

## Proposed fix
In start()'s Web Speech branch, guard against a stop() that raced the getUserMedia await. Capture the intended recognition instance before the await and, after `await this.startAudioLevelMonitoring()`, detect supersession: `if (this.recognition !== recognition) { this.stopAudioLevelMonitoring(); return { started: false }; }` before calling recognition.start(). This releases the level-meter stream/interval that startAudioLevelMonitoring created during the await and avoids starting an unreferenceable recognizer. (Equivalently, a monotonically increasing startToken/`stopping` flag set by stop() and checked after the await.) Scope is ~4 lines in one file, no contract change. Test plan (>=10 lines, extends existing web.test.ts harness): (1) race teardown — deferred getUserMedia, call start() then stop() before resolving, resolve the stream, assert isListening() false, the FakeRecognition never left running, and the mic track.stop spy was called; (2) normal path preserved — start() fully awaited then a valid final speech result still emits transcript/wakeWord and isListening() true; (3) idempotency — a second stop() after the race does not throw. All assertions run against the real SwabbleWeb, no stubbing of the unit under test.

## Evidence plan
The PR will attach failing-before/passing-after vitest output for the new race test in plugins/plugin-native-swabble/src/web.test.ts (before: isListening()==={listening:true}, recognition running, mic track.stop never called; after: {listening:false}, recognition not running, mic track stopped), plus `bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-native-swabble test` (all existing tests still green), typecheck, and lint. It will show the regression test for the normal awaited start→speech→stop path remains green to prove no behavior change for correct callers.

gh search issues --repo elizaOS/eliza: "swabble stop race" (0), "SwabbleWeb start stop" (0), "swabble startAudioLevelMonitoring" (0), "swabble recognition running after stop" (0), "swabble microphone leak" → only #22655 (CLOSED). My defect never triggers onerror/onend — recognition.start() succeeds and keeps running — so it is not covered by #22656. No issue/PR describes the start()/stop() interleave race.

#28408 broadened `keepAliveAfterComplete` to ordinary durable Smithers sessions so they can accept follow-ups. The retained ACP session becomes `ready`, while its durable owner task remains terminal. Two existing lifecycle consumers interpret that split state unsafely:

1. **The watchdog treats intentional promptable idle as stalled work.** `detectStalledSessions` excludes only terminal ACP statuses, so a retained `ready` session crosses the default three-minute threshold and receives `STALL_GRILL_PROMPT`. That creates an unsolicited model turn after completed work; because activity refreshes and the dedupe set can clear, the cycle can repeat.
2. **Capacity reclamation can stop an in-flight follow-up.** `reclaimIdleSession` also excludes only terminal ACP statuses. A follow-up changes the ACP session to `busy`, but its durable owner task is still terminal, so queue pressure can select and stop that busy session.

The merge commit [`0cc958b7`](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/commit/0cc958b7ca9cb8ecbd377c99fd3bcdd02d976ee4) is an ancestor of current `develop` [`e68ba2e8`](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/commit/e68ba2e84ee09a0b5cb6c6a4b7e03861be295ba0). The relevant production blobs are byte-identical between them.

## Current code path

- Durable Smithers retention is enabled in [`TASKS:create`](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/e68ba2e84ee09a0b5cb6c6a4b7e03861be295ba0/plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator/src/actions/tasks.ts#L909-L919).
- A completed retained prompt returns to [`ready`](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/e68ba2e84ee09a0b5cb6c6a4b7e03861be295ba0/plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator/src/services/acp-service.ts#L3755-L3759).
- The watchdog filters only terminal states, then sends the grill prompt to every stale candidate ([detector](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/e68ba2e84ee09a0b5cb6c6a4b7e03861be295ba0/plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator/src/services/task-watchdog-service.ts#L62-L77), [dispatch](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/e68ba2e84ee09a0b5cb6c6a4b7e03861be295ba0/plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator/src/services/task-watchdog-service.ts#L272-L300)).
- A follow-up becomes [`busy`](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/e68ba2e84ee09a0b5cb6c6a4b7e03861be295ba0/plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator/src/services/acp-service.ts#L2498-L2516), but the reclaimer still accepts every nonterminal ACP state and stops the selected session ([reclaimer](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/e68ba2e84ee09a0b5cb6c6a4b7e03861be295ba0/plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator/src/services/orchestrator-task-service.ts#L7274-L7313)).

a2:Tcf1,## Defect

The observed staging incident is a stale-enabled orphan reconciler, not the provision catch path. Four healthy generations with the same deterministic name were removed by direct Docker force-removal-shaped events after the reconciler five-minute grace window, despite terminal lifecycle jobs and fresh heartbeats. The deploy preserves `/opt/eliza/cloud/.env.local`, so an old `ORPHAN_RECONCILER_ENABLED=1` survives even though the daemon code defaults the feature off.

A separate code-proven latent race exists in post-create failure cleanup: the provision catch retains an exact Docker handle but discards its immutable container ID and replacement attempt when it falls back to `stopForReplacement(handle.sandboxId)`. Because the sandbox ID is the reusable container name, delayed cleanup can resolve a healthy successor.

## Production-like evidence

One staging sandbox produced four healthy same-name containers with distinct immutable Docker IDs and `ai.elizaos.replacement-attempt` labels. Docker delivered direct signal 9 events with no preceding stop/SIGTERM after each container had exceeded the five-minute grace window.

The fourth generation started at 23:57:14Z, wrote a fresh serving-row update at 00:03:51Z, then received signal 9 at 00:04:07Z and was destroyed at 00:04:08Z, about 412 seconds after start. Its database row was still `running`, carried the expected node and VPN address, and no destructive lifecycle job was active. A node-health sweep had updated at 00:03:13Z; the kill followed about 54 seconds later. The preceding generation had the same `sweep + 54 seconds -> SIGKILL` shape. This is the orphan phase signature, although the underlying read-authority mismatch that classified a live row as orphaned still requires separate investigation.

## Scope

- Make the provisioning-worker deploy overwrite stale host state with repository-owned `ORPHAN_RECONCILER_ENABLED=0`, verify it before restart, and verify it again in the health gate.
- Route failed Docker provision cleanup through its exact node, immutable container ID, replacement attempt, and VPN identity.
- Validate the expected agent/container identity and fail closed when exact Docker cleanup identity is incomplete.
- Preserve mutable sandbox-ID cleanup only for non-Docker providers.
- Do not add or mutate database schema.

## Acceptance

- A deploy rewrites a seeded host `ORPHAN_RECONCILER_ENABLED=1` to exactly one `ORPHAN_RECONCILER_ENABLED=0` entry and refuses health if it drifts.
- A stale cleanup for an old Docker ID cannot stop or remove a healthy successor that reuses the same container name.
- Cleanup still stops/removes the exact target when its immutable ID and attempt label match.
- Retry/absence stays idempotent and never targets the current name occupant.
- Focused cloud-shared and deployment reconciliation tests, typecheck, and Biome pass.

## Evidence plan

- Execute the deployment `EnvironmentFile` block verbatim against a stale seeded host file.
- Drive the real Docker identity resolver and scripted SSH transport across same-name reuse.
- Prove at service level that the provision catch passes exact handle identity and never invokes mutable-name Docker teardown.
- N/A UI, frontend, LLM, audio, and visual evidence: backend lifecycle and deployment configuration only.

b0:T173d,Closes #29117

## Summary

- recover built-in app routes across deferred runtime boot instead of caching an early 404 as permanent unavailability
- route Settings, Wallet, Calendar, Notes, Browser, Knowledge, Memories, and Trajectories through a shared responsive workspace/layout system
- scope view caches and reloads to the active agent authority so switching between local, Shared, and Dedicated agents cannot leak stale capability state
- remount Knowledge, Memories, and Trajectories at the authority boundary and cancel delayed or in-flight warm-up work so an agent switch cannot render, request, or cache the prior agent's data
- make deferred readiness route-specific: a live runtime route or direct host handler remains reachable even if unrelated late boot work is still pending or fails
- keep Android's build-pinned remote target fail-closed even when a pre-built UI constructs the shared client before the app publishes its compiled target; stale Cloud sockets, bases, and bearers are retired before bootstrap awaits
- expose the active agent's EVM and Solana public addresses in Wallet, with the EVM address shared across every supported EVM chain
- make Shared-agent capability boundaries explicit and typed instead of rendering broken or retry-looping views
- consolidate Settings navigation, rows, controls, connector states, error states, and mobile/desktop framing onto reusable UI primitives
- preserve overlay-aware geometry and chat clearance across Browser, Pendant, Experience, Files, fullscreen plugin pages, and ambient Cloud routes

## Runtime capability boundary

| View | Local / Dedicated | Shared |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wallet public addresses | Supported | Supported through the Steward wallet proxy |
| Memories | Supported | Supported through the durable Shared-memory adapter |
| Permissions read | Supported | Returns the honest empty capability set |
| Browser | Supported where the native browser surface exists | Typed non-retryable Dedicated-required state |
| Calendar | Supported | Typed non-retryable Dedicated-required state |
| Notes | Supported | Typed non-retryable Dedicated-required state |
| Knowledge / Documents | Supported | Typed non-retryable Dedicated-required state |
| Trajectories | Supported | Typed non-retryable Dedicated-required state |

This PR does not pretend that isolated plugin runtimes exist on Shared agents. It fixes false cold-boot unavailability and presents true runtime boundaries clearly.

b1:T80b,## Scope

Adds the private Agent filesystem boundary needed to stage an exact restore-v3 candidate for #20726. The implementation is split into authority/control, durable JSON, payload, and tree proof/cleanup modules behind one small facade.

This PR does not materialize PGlite/character/media/state/vault components, boot a candidate, publish activation, or route traffic.

## Guarantees

- production is Linux-only and descriptor-bound through `/proc/self/fd`; every traversed directory is opened `O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW`
- one persistent kernel `flock` remains bound to the attempt-root inode across pathname rename
- payload owner/receipt sidecars allow exact crash and lost-response replay without persisting the owner token itself
- canonical durable JSON uses no-replace link publication plus parent-directory fsync and exact crash repair
- payloads reject symlinks, hardlinks, overflow, replaced inodes, and other owners; provider-owned buffers/descriptors are disposed on late abort
- canonical JSON rejects sparse arrays, accessors, symbol keys, and undeclared properties
- cleanup preflights the bounded tree and uses an internal cleanup deadline
- non-Linux pathname emulation is available only with the explicit test-only flag under `NODE_ENV=test`; production fails closed

## Proof

- Linux container with real `/proc` and kernel flock: 15/15, 59 assertions
- macOS explicit test-only emulation: 15/15, 59 assertions
- Agent TypeScript: green
- Biome: green
- git diff --check: green
- no residual test container or flock/sleep helper

## Explicit platform limit

`flock` is advisory for cooperative participants. Node does not expose the full `openat2`/`unlinkat`/`linkat(AT_EMPTY_PATH)` set used to eliminate every last-component race against a deliberately non-cooperative same-UID process. Ancestors remain descriptor-bound/no-follow and final identities are revalidated; deployments must keep the staging root private to this Agent authority.

Draft only. Keep stacked on #29958; do not mark Ready or merge without explicit authorization.b2:T119f,Follow-up to #28281 and the merged canonical atom work.

## What this changes

- adds a build-time design dependency graph across tokens, atoms, inferred molecules, declared organisms, and page shells
- fails closed when a reusable molecule or any reachable helper claims raw paint or interaction capability
- keeps an exact zero-entry debt ledger, so new findings fail immediately and stale debt also fails in tight mode
- migrates shared UI and plugin compositions to canonical atoms and typed variants
- adds deterministic molecule ownership, consumer, rendered-tag, and atomic-dependency contracts

b6:T51d,## Scope

Adds one exact, bounded multipart object primitive for Workers R2 and explicit S3-compatible providers, for the Sandboxes V2 restore/publication path in #20726.

This PR intentionally does not add durable multipart publication state, generation-wide failover, survivor repair, boot, activation, or routing.

## Guarantees

- fixed 8 MiB parts, at most 128 parts / 1 GiB, and keys bounded to 1024 UTF-8 bytes
- at most one provider-owned part buffer per session; admission occurs before the copy and bytes are zeroized after settlement
- mandatory bounded deadline, cancellation, and late-settlement registration
- create is never retried after an indeterminate response; late handles are bounded-aborted
- exact part replay and complete-response-loss reconciliation by drained HEAD plus GET
- S3 crash recovery adopts only an exact completed object after NoSuchUpload; drift and absence fail closed
- private provider handles remain non-enumerable and rehydrate only against the exact configured backend

## Proof

- multipart targeted suite: 17/17, 217 assertions
- complete cloud/shared storage directory: 65/65, 451 assertions
- cloud shared TypeScript: green
- Biome: green
- git diff --check: green

# Stable request contract

Both request routes accept:

```ts
{

  admissionCredential: string; // exactly 32 random bytes encoded as 43-character base64url
}
```

Clients must persist `admissionCredential` before the first POST, reuse it after transport failure, and remove it only after accepted status/recovery capabilities are validated and persisted. The shared type is `AccountDeletionRequestBodyDto`.

Routes:

- `GET|POST /api/v1/me/account-deletion`
- `POST /api/public/account-deletion`
- `POST /api/public/account-deletion/status`
- `POST /api/public/account-deletion/cancel`
- `POST /api/public/account-deletion/export`

bd:T1d8c,## Summary

Telegram membership-authority vertical slice for #23101: the Telegram connector's join (`new_chat_members`) / leave (`left_chat_member`) / kick event paths and inbound group-message admission are wired into the canonical `MembershipService` authority (landed in #25379/#25474/#25514), proving same-turn revocation and fail-closed admission when the authority is stale, unavailable, or its writes fail.

Refs #23101 (kept open — this is the first connector slice of the multi-connector security architecture).

## What this PR does

- **`plugins/plugin-telegram/src/membership.ts`** — `TelegramMembershipAuthority`: per-(agent, account) authority client. Typed idempotent evidence commands from Telegram updates (deterministic idempotency keys, point-query evidence mode, TTL validity), out-of-order protection (strict same-second tie-break against resurrection), publisher fencing with adopt-and-retry on cursor/generation mismatches, bot-removal tombstones + re-add watermarks, restart hydration of persisted scope state, and a durable pending-revocation overlay for revocations whose evidence write failed.
- **`plugins/plugin-telegram/src/membership-gate.ts`** — the admission gate bound into `MessageManager`: every group message is gated BEFORE `processMessage`; denied principals reconcile via `getChatMember` and are re-checked; authority unavailability fails closed (`TELEGRAM_MEMBERSHIP_ENFORCE=1` strict, default degrade-allow+warn for non-sql deployments).
- **`plugins/plugin-telegram/src/service.ts` / `messageManager.ts`** — event wiring for join/leave/kick/bot-removal, connector-removal suspension, and the gate-before-processing ordering.
- **`plugins/plugin-sql/src/services/sql-membership.ts`** — one-line subject-scope fix in the reconcile path.

## Security invariants (all execution-proven, see tests)

1. **Same-turn revocation**: read → leave evidence → read denies (`membership_revoked`).
2. **Out-of-order/duplicate redelivery cannot resurrect** a committed revocation (strict same-second tie-break; distinct-message-id old joins skipped).
3. **Failed revocation writes fail closed**: the scope degrades stale AND a per-principal overlay fence installs atomically inside the same per-scope serialized chain link — a queued authorize cannot overtake the fence. The fence is durable (runtime cache) and survives restart even after unrelated evidence restores scope health.
4. **Cache outages fail closed**: an unreadable durable overlay denies admission (never consults possibly-stale active evidence); an unwritable fence escalates to gate-broken (every group admission fails closed).
5. **Never rewrites the durable overlay from an unhydrated set** — an unrelated evidence commit during a cache outage cannot erase other principals' revocation fences.
6. **Bot removal tombstones** the scope: backlogged evidence after removal cannot restore authority; only an explicit re-add (with a watermark suppressing pre-re-add observations) can.
7. **Reconcile subject-mismatch** (provider response describing a different user than requested) is rejected.

Real-runtime PGlite suite (`vitest.real-runtime.config.ts`, real `AgentRuntime` + real `SqlMembershipService`, fault-injected outages on the real instances): **14/14 pass**, including:
- join/leave admission, getChatMember backfill reconcile, kicked reconcile deny
- duplicate redelivery + older-join non-resurrection + same-second tie-break
- restart publisher-binding continuation, restart tombstone hydration
- fault-injected pending revocation: overlay deny across unrelated-evidence health restore, **restart durability** (RED on parent: re-authorized), **queued-authorize overtake race** (RED on parent: admitted), **cache-outage fail-closed + recovery**, **unhydrated-set fence erasure** (restart scenario, RED on parent: fence erased).

# Risks

Medium. This adds 18 PostgreSQL migrations and a narrowly marked nontransactional migration mode for online concurrent indexes. A defect could rewrite existing data, block hot writers, admit forged work, or publish the wrong index identity. The implementation keeps each schema migration below 100 lines, validates exact PostgreSQL-canonical index definitions and OIDs, fails closed on incomplete remnants without live-table repair DDL, and publishes markers plus the migration ledger only after final table/index locks and post-lock identity/ownership checks.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

This PR adds the durable authority required before a fair backup scheduler can enroll or claim work:

- write-once sandbox and node source identity plus snapshot visibility fencing;
- frozen enrollment cohorts, monotonic claim turns, priority passes, and shard authorities;
- tenant-bound admission work with explicit queued/deferred/leased/settled states, replay identity, lease fencing, and guarded deletion;
- durable queued-to-leased admission proofs bound to the exact transaction, cycle, shard, pass, attempt, high-water mark, and live lease before a claim cycle can restart;
- bounded claim/deferred/expired-lease indexes and exact hot-catalogue lane-conflict indexes;
- an explicit one-statement `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` migration path with canonical definition checks, fail-closed crash remnants, same-name race rejection, final publication locks, and atomic marker/ledger publication;
- Drizzle schema parity and full account-deletion FK classification;
- metadata-only GC admission reuse without rewriting existing GC rows.

There is intentionally no production repository, producer, caller, or `agent_backup_admission_work` insertion in this slice. The next enrollment PR is the first producer and must settle all admission work before irreversible account deletion. The following claim PR owns the 10,000-due-agent drain/fairness and zero-oversubscription proof.

Feature foundation and database integrity improvement.

c3:T273a,# feat(billing): expose provider-neutral payment states in billing UI

Closes #22966

## What this does

Extends the Billing surface with a server-authoritative, read-only projection of purchase payment states — unifying #22427's provider-neutral receipts, Stripe checkout orders, and the refund/dispute clawback+reinstatement credit ledger:

- **`PaymentHistoryService.listPaymentStates`** (`packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/payment-history.ts`): org-scoped projection with typed purchase identity (Stripe payment-intent unification; OxaPay joins via `payment_request_id` — synthetic grant keys can never collide with a real Stripe intent, so no cross-provider reversal leakage).
- **`GET /api/v1/billing/payment-states`** (`packages/cloud/api/v1/billing/payment-states/route.ts`): org-auth + standard rate limit, bounded pagination, J1 boundary translation.
- **`PaymentActivityCard`** (`packages/ui/src/cloud/billing/components/payment-activity-card.tsx`): distinct loading / empty / error-with-retry / success / unavailable states; status never conveyed by color alone (icon + verbatim state text); credit amounts labeled as credits, never formatted as currency. Each row links to its payment detail.
- **Linked order/receipt detail (#22966 review r3–r5)**: `GET /api/v1/billing/payment-states/:id` (org-scoped lookup over the same projection — id validated (`{surface}:{authority}` shape, length ≤ 200) before any service call; real 404 when the row is outside the org's bounded history window; lossless offset paging since r5 — see the superseded r4 note below) + `cloud/billing/payments/:id` (`PaymentStateDetailPage`, registered specific-before-general) with loading / not-found / error-with-retry / success states, full-shape payload validation (a partial row is an explicit error, never a fabricated render), typed `ApiError.status === 404` branching, and the full identifiers (not truncated) with copy affordances + J4 clipboard degrade.

### Authority model

| Fact | Authority |
|---|---|
| Settled purchase (amount, currency, provider, settlement time) | immutable `payment_request_receipts` row (#22427) |
| Settled request without receipt | explicit `unavailable` — never a fabricated success |
| Legacy checkout orders (no receipt possible) | durable server order row |
| Refund/dispute cumulative USD | per-authority max snapshot (charge.id / dispute.id), then summed across authorities — Stripe's cumulative semantics, no replay double-count |
| Applied clawback / reinstatement | credit units (ledger row amounts), kept separate from provider USD |
| Unrecovered balance shortfall | explicit amber line from the clawback mutation's recorded shortfall |
| Policy effect | always `unavailable` + reason while #22930 (refund entitlement policy) is unresolved — never a guessed outcome |
| Reversal association | receipt `provider` + `provider_tx_ref` when a receipt exists (immutable); mutable request row is legacy fallback only |

### Tests (all green at head)

- **44 pglite service tests** (`payment-history.pglite.test.ts`, 413 `expect()` calls) — real schema, real SQL: base states incl. `expired`, org isolation, provider isolation (OxaPay↔Stripe), replay (unique ledger index rejects duplicate insert — DrizzleQueryError cause-chain walk, probe-proven), partial-after-consumption, dispute withdraw→reinstate ordering, two-tab checkout, lost post-payment response, receipt-vs-request divergence (amount/currency/time AND reversal association), stale-ref non-attachment control.
- **21 UI vitest tests** across `payment-activity-card.test.tsx` (row links: exact `href` + action-specific accessible names under a real router) and `PaymentStateDetailPage.test.tsx` (loading / not-found / error+retry / malformed / partial-payload drop-one-field ×8 / full-row rendering / copy identifiers / reversal totals / no-receipt honesty).
- **8 route tests** across `payment-states-detail-route.test.ts` + `payment-states-list-route.test.ts` — org's own row by stable projection id, 404 outside the window, tenant isolation (ORG_A vs ORG_B), 400 on malformed ids before any service call.
- Full billing UI directory regression: **17 files / 286 tests green** at head.

# Risks

Medium. Claiming coordinates concurrent workers across 64 shards and strict tenant/node lanes. A defect could duplicate leases, starve a shard, cross an expired fence, or violate priority ordering. Durable frozen recovery cursors, trigger guards, post-lock database time, exact generation/attempt fences, and bounded `SKIP LOCKED` scans constrain those risks.

# What does this PR do?

- Claims queued `schedule_capture / reserve_capture` work with strict business-priority passes.
- Uses maximum-cardinality tenant/node lane matching without deriving authority from opaque work UUIDs.
- Adds durable, monotone recovery high-water/cursor state for deferred and expired work.
- Advances recovery and shard service turns even when raw rows are locked, preserving cross-shard fairness.
- Fences heartbeat, defer, and settlement against the exact live generation, attempt, cycle, and post-lock database clock.
- Adds real PostgreSQL and PGlite coverage, including 10,000 due rows plus 640 arrivals across all 64 shards.
- Performs database-only admission changes; capacity/autoscale/provider sentinels remain unchanged.

Closes #24371

Replaces the removed third-party proxy transport with direct first-party WeChat paths: Official Account (MP) and WeCom self-built apps over the official platform APIs — signature-verified public callback server, official customer-service/app-message sends, no proxy.

## What changes

- **Direct transports** — `api-client.ts` / `token-manager.ts` (account-scoped access tokens, single-flight) send through fixed `api.weixin.qq.com` / `qyapi.weixin.qq.com` hosts; personal/proxy/wecom-third-party modes rejected with typed errors; legacy `WECHAT_API_KEY`/`WECHAT_PROXY_URL` fail with `WECHAT_PROXY_CONFIG_UNSUPPORTED`.
- **Callback boundary** — `callback-server.ts` + `callback-crypto.ts`: SHA-1 signature verification before any parsing; AES-256-CBC encrypted mode with Tencent's 32-byte PKCS#7 scheme; receiver-id binding (corpId / gh_ original ID — never appId); per-account path addressing so a ciphertext signed for one account is never accepted for another.
- **Hardened XML** — `xml.ts` flat parser (CDATA leaves, no DTD/entities/nesting/duplicate roots), parsed only after signature verification.
- **Connector + account provider** — targets derived exclusively from signature-verified inbound senders (no roster API on these platforms); observational account status (connected requires a real first-party observation).
- **Tests** — 16 new tests across 6 suites (config resolution, callback boundary with real listeners, crypto with official Tencent vectors, UTF-8 chunk-boundary integrity, token lifecycle, provider), all with RED controls per review round.

## Key invariants

- Signature verification precedes payload parsing; encrypted-mode accounts cannot be downgraded to the plaintext path by request shape.
- Outbound receipts are enforced: platform rejection, non-zero errcode, or unparseable body is a failed send — never a fabricated success.
- Replay expiry aligns with the timestamp freshness endpoint (r5 fix).

# Risks

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Preserves locally owned optimistic message lineage after terminal receipts replace temporary row IDs. A stale independently running history request can therefore merge without deleting the just-rekeyed user and assistant rows; later durable history still converges without duplicates.

The source fix is deliberately narrow: local ownership now follows a temporary `id` **or** a preserved temporary `clientRenderId`. Conversation ownership and server-ID deduplication remain unchanged. The PR also extends the deterministic browser regression fixture and its CI workflow coverage.

Provenance reviewed:

- #26176 and its reconciliation regression coverage: @NubsCarson / nubs;
- the original conversation-history loader and terminal rekey paths: @Shaw.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking).

# Documentation changes needed?

No project documentation change is needed. The browser fixture and regression tests document the contract directly.

# Risks

Medium, isolated to database schema and the not-yet-consumed replacement-attempt repository surface. The migration adds an owner-lifetime append-only authority table, constraints, partial unique indexes, immutability/state-transition triggers, and a composite foreign key to the exact append-only Docker-node occurrence.

The occurrence tuple is `(history id, Docker-node record id, node incarnation)`, rather than the incarnation UUID alone, so node rotation and ABA reuse fail closed. Direct row deletion and truncation remain forbidden. An organization-owned cascade is allowed only for terminal non-restore history; active replacement effects abort the entire organization deletion. Existing restore-backed retention authorities can still reject organization deletion.

This PR does not deploy or apply the migration to a live database. If #25372 or the migration tail changes first, this branch must be restacked, renumbered, and revalidated before merge.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Adds the missing SQL migration and journal registration for the already-defined `agent_sandbox_replacement_attempts` schema/repository, then binds every durable replacement locator to one exact Docker-node occurrence.

The table:

- fences duplicate provider effects by active agent and activation generation;
- binds optional restore-lease provenance;
- enforces complete locator and receipt shapes;
- preserves the exact node occurrence across rotation and ABA reuse;
- revalidates and locks the current Docker-node occurrence before placement/adoption;
- retains attempt history for the owner's lifetime;
- permits terminal non-restore erasure only through the owning organization cascade, while unresolved/provider-succeeded effects block that erasure atomically.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature / database migration substrate.

# Documentation changes needed?

No external documentation change is required. The migration, repository contract, and tests document the state machine and authority tuple directly; runtime consumption will be reviewed separately.

# Risks

Medium. Traffic fence is deliberately fail-open for scopes with no installation record (existing installs keep working); only terminal-state records (`removed`/`revoked`/`failed`) stop traffic, which is exactly the issue criterion ("removal stops traffic"). Scope-creep guard: no database migration, no API routes, no UI changes.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Implements the first tranche of the canonical invite-to-ready group installation lifecycle (#23107):

1. **Durable provider-neutral state machine** (`packages/core/src/messaging/installation-lifecycle.ts`): an account-scoped installation record joining provider invite, external group, required scopes, single-use expiring owner claim, runtime room binding, readiness state, removal, and reinstall versioning. States: `invite_created → provider_authorized → agent_joined → permissions_verifying → owner_claim_pending → ready`, with terminal `degraded`/`removed`/`revoked`/`failed`. Signed-event normalization: events are tenant-bound, idempotent, replay-safe (terminal receipt replay is a no-op), and epoch-guarded (future `reinstallVersion` epochs rejected; stale epochs rejected; equal-epoch reapply rejects wrong-secret attempts and persists attempt burning to exhaustion).
2. **Connector contribution contract** (`packages/core/src/messaging/installation-contribution.ts` + `installation-service.ts`): the contract a connector implements — install/deep-link shape, group types, scope requirements, signed event normalization, readiness proof, uninstall, provider-specific activation. `InstallationLifecycleService` registers contributions per `(agentId, connectorId)`.
3. **Discord pilot adapter** (`plugins/plugin-discord/installation-adapter.ts`, `discord-events.ts`, `index.ts`, `messages.ts`): canonical permission catalog (tiered invite URL activation), guildCreate/guildDelete normalization (unknown shapes refused), owner-claim handoff that never exposes tokens in the group, and the gateway-boundary fence — a fenced (removed/revoked/failed) guild skips `handleGuildCreate` at the event-listener seam and stops message traffic at the message-send seam.

## What kind of change is this?

Features (non-breaking change which adds functionality).

# Documentation changes needed?

My changes do not require a change to the project documentation (contract is documented in code headers; user-facing install UX arrives with the next tranche's install-URL surface).

2. `plugins/plugin-discord/__tests__/installation-adapter.test.ts` — contribution shape (permission catalog, tiered invite URLs), event normalization (unknown shapes refused), traffic gate semantics.
3. `plugins/plugin-discord/__tests__/installation-gateway-boundary.test.ts` — the fence at the real `setupDiscordEventListeners` seam: a fenced guild never reaches `handleGuildCreate`.
4. `plugins/plugin-discord/__tests__/installation-contribution-init.test.ts` — plugin init registers the contribution against the real core service.

d4:T177c,## Summary

Closes #22961. Adds a single settlement authority for MCP purchases: one authoritative receipt row per economic event, first-committed-wins with replay-mismatch rejection, every payout leg applied exactly once under settlement-scoped idempotency keys, and a durable recovery lane on the credit-reservation cron that resumes wedged receipts and refunds orphaned precharges.

- `mcp_settlements` receipt table: `(payment_type, payment_event_id)` is the canonical identity of one purchase; replay of the same event lands on the committed row, replay with different economics throws.
- Every leg (creator org credit, creator redeemable earnings, affiliate earnings, usage row + stats) keys its idempotency on the settlement receipt, so re-driving a delivery — retry, concurrent duplicate, or sweep resume — is exactly-once.
- Claim-timestamp ownership protocol on the buyer debit (`mcp_precharge_swept` + `mcp_precharge_swept_at`): the live delivery and the recovery sweep claim the same row through mutually exclusive single-row UPDATEs; staleness is judged by when the claim was written, never by the debit's age; a failed sweep refund stays retryable until the refund commits; the deducting `recordUsage` path tags its debit for the same recovery.
- Balanced-ledger suite proves conservation of value across retries, concurrent delivery, crash-recovery, sweep/late-delivery races, and refund-retry — 23 tests, each new race RED-proven against the prior commit before being fixed.

## What is deliberately NOT changed

The dual creator-credit legs (creator org credit + creator redeemable earnings from one purchase) are preserved exactly as they behave today — no money flow is altered by this PR. The open economic-policy question was posted on the issue (2026-08-23): each leg is independently keyed to the receipt, so a ruling to drop one leg is a one-line change gated on the same linkage. Tracking: #22942 parent audit.

## Evidence

- Balanced-ledger suite: `bun test --isolate ./packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/__tests__/mcp-settlement-balanced-ledger.test.ts` — 23/23 pass, covering single delivery, retry, concurrent duplicate, unkeyed settlement, replay mismatch, partial-leg recovery, sweep refund of orphans, late-delivery-after-refund refusal, crashed-live-claim redelivery, dead-claim reclaim after horizon, stale-claim vs sweep race, refunding-window refusal, failed-refund retry-exactly-once, deducting-path crash recovery, and the mid-delivery sweep race on an old debit.
- Numeric conservation suite: `user-mcps-recordusage-numeric.test.ts` — 17/17 pass.
- RED controls (fix-removed, test-only runs at the prior commits): round-6 tests fail 3/3 on round-5 code; the round-7 mid-delivery race test fails on round-6 code (sweep refunds mid-delivery; delivery settles a refunded debit).

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Advertises an `exact-success` replacement capability with a caller-owned, one-shot UUID and ordered start → intent → Docker-created → VPN-enriched → success-only settlement callbacks.
- Freezes exact Docker-node authority as the immutable DB record UUID plus hostname, SSH port/user, and host-key pin; replay resolves on the primary by record UUID and rejects authority drift before SSH.
- Adds a remote `flock`/tombstone protocol, active-producer marker, durable candidate-ID receipt, and deterministic cleanup of six temporary secret paths. Ambiguous or late Docker outcomes remain fenced.
- Makes exact Headscale cleanup ID-authoritative with strict inventory proof and binds the API registration IP to the exact Docker container's Tailscale IP.
- Tracks ambiguous registry/autoscale completion and prevents a success callback after unresolved remote mutation.
- Preserves the real legacy `ElizaSandboxService` intent/created/VPN callback contract without requiring the new exact tuple.

If an exact locator has a Docker container ID and Headscale registration metadata but no durable Headscale node ID, cleanup remains `in_flight_unresolved`; polling by name cannot prove absence against a late Headscale POST. If Docker start was never reached (`containerId === null` under the strict stage contract), cleanup can safely omit Headscale.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix and provider-side prerequisite for the remaining #22947 admission work.

# Documentation changes needed?

No external documentation change is required. The public provider types contain the exact consumer contract and explicitly state that Slice S must add durable consumer persistence, append-only migration, node-authority revalidation/locking, and the final CAS.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Advertises an `exact-success` replacement capability with a caller-owned, one-shot UUID and ordered start → intent → Docker-created → VPN-enriched → success-only settlement callbacks.
- Freezes exact Docker-node authority as the immutable DB record UUID plus hostname, SSH port/user, and host-key pin; replay resolves on the primary by record UUID and rejects authority drift before SSH.
- Adds a remote `flock`/tombstone protocol, active-producer marker, durable candidate-ID receipt, and deterministic cleanup of six temporary secret paths. Ambiguous or late Docker outcomes remain fenced.
- Makes exact Headscale cleanup ID-authoritative with strict inventory proof and binds the API registration IP to the exact Docker container's Tailscale IP.
- Tracks ambiguous registry/autoscale completion and prevents a success callback after unresolved remote mutation.
- Preserves the real legacy `ElizaSandboxService` intent/created/VPN callback contract without requiring the new exact tuple.

If an exact locator has a Docker container ID and Headscale registration metadata but no durable Headscale node ID, cleanup remains `in_flight_unresolved`; polling by name cannot prove absence against a late Headscale POST. If Docker start was never reached (`containerId === null` under the strict stage contract), cleanup can safely omit Headscale.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix and provider-side prerequisite for the remaining #22947 admission work.

# Documentation changes needed?

No external documentation change is required. The public provider types contain the exact consumer contract and explicitly state that Slice S must add durable consumer persistence, append-only migration, node-authority revalidation/locking, and the final CAS.

<!-- eliza-computer-attribution:v1 {"provider":"openai","model":"gpt-5.6","client":"Codex Desktop","skill_revision":"N/A - contribution skill unavailable in this session"} -->d7:T16d7,## What

Adds structural server management to the stock Discord connector, exposed through the production `MESSAGE` tool as `op=manage_server` (`source=discord`). This wires the previously declared-but-unimplemented `DiscordActionConfig` gates (`channels`, `roles`, `permissions`, `moderation`) to real, bounded operations so an agent can build and maintain a Discord server from ordinary chat instructions.

### Verbs

- `create_category`, `create_channel`, `edit_channel`, `delete_channel`
- `create_role`, `edit_role`, `delete_role`
- `edit_permissions` (channel permission overwrites, role/user/@everyone subject)
- `assign_role`, `remove_role`
- `create_invite`
- `kick`, `ban`, `unban`, `timeout`
- `list_templates`, `apply_template` (idempotent template reconcile)

## Security gates (fail closed)

- Every structural write requires the corresponding `settings.discord.actions.channels|roles|permissions|moderation` gate to be **explicitly `true`**. Absent config = OFF. Truthy non-boolean values (e.g. the string `"true"`) also stay OFF. Env fallbacks (`DISCORD_ACTIONS_*`) are consulted only when the config key is absent. `apply_template` requires channels + roles + permissions together.
- **Role hierarchy enforced**: only roles strictly below the bot's highest role can be edited/deleted/assigned; integration-managed roles and `@everyone` are refused; kick/ban/timeout honor `kickable`/`bannable`/`moderatable` and refuse the guild owner.
- **No admin bypass**: granting `Administrator` through any role or overwrite is always rejected, and requested permissions must be a subset of what the bot itself holds (no escalation).
- Guild/channel ownership validated (`CHANNEL_WRONG_GUILD`, `CHANNEL_NOT_FOUND`, `MEMBER_NOT_FOUND`); the bot's own Discord-side permission (`ManageChannels`, `ManageRoles`, `CreateInstantInvite`, `KickMembers`, `BanMembers`, `ModerateMembers`) is checked per verb with an actionable re-invite message.
- Bounded inputs: name/topic/permission-list/overwrite-count limits, hex color validation, invite age clamped to 7 days, timeout clamped to 28 days, ban delete-window clamped to 7 days. Unknown permission names are rejected by name. No tokens in any output.

## Non-destructive template reconcile

`apply_template` reconciles a declarative guild spec (roles -> categories -> channels -> overwrites, deterministic order) against the live guild:

- Objects match by **stable template key** via a persisted key->snowflake map (runtime cache, per account+guild+template), with exact-name fallback, so re-apply converges to `unchanged` instead of duplicating.
- Managed-field drift (name, topic, parent, color, hoist, mentionable, permissions, overwrites) is corrected; **unmanaged channels and roles are NEVER deleted**. Deletion exists only as the explicit gated `delete_channel`/`delete_role` verbs.
- `dryRun: true` returns the full plan (`would_create`/`would_update`) without touching Discord — on every verb, not just templates.
- Four vendor-neutral built-in templates ship as plugin assets: `companion-private`, `friends-casual`, `project-team`, `community-public`. Deployments extend/override via `settings.discord.guildTemplates` (per-account override supported). `{{agent}}` renders the character name.
- Every operation returns a structured receipt listing created/updated/unchanged/skipped entities plus a human summary.

## Tool path

`plugin-discord` still registers `actions: []`. The surface rides the existing message-connector contract:

- `packages/core/src/types/runtime.ts`: new optional `manageServerHandler` connector hook + `manage_server` capability + param/result types.
- `packages/core/src/features/advanced-capabilities/actions/message.ts`: new `manage_server` op with natural-language verb aliases (`create_channel`, `apply_template`, `kick_member`, ...), bounded param forwarding (allowlisted keys only), and `MESSAGE_PARAMETERS` schema entries for discoverability.
- `plugins/plugin-discord/service.ts`: `manageConnectorServer` adapts the live guild to the management module and registers the hook per account (multi-account scoping preserved).
- `plugins/plugin-discord/guild-management.ts` / `guild-templates.ts`: the management engine operates on narrow structural interfaces so tests drive it with plain fakes.

## Config defaults

```json
{
  "settings": {
    "discord": {
      "token": "<bot token>",
      "actions": { "channels": true, "roles": true, "permissions": true, "moderation": false }
    }
  }
}
```

Default remains everything OFF; the snippet above is the opt-in example documented in the README.

Fixes #25518. Refs #25268, #26821, and #22896.db:T18fc,# feat(core,plugin-sql): native paging for large messages and attachment text (#25140)

Closes #25140

Adds native content segmentation and paging so large message bodies and attachment text are stored as revision-fenced segments and paged on demand, instead of being written and read as single unbounded rows.

## What changes

- **`packages/core/src/memory/content-segmentation.ts` (new)** — segmentation contracts: bounded segment emission, surrogate-safe boundaries, deterministic segment identity; 14 unit tests.
- **`core memory.ts` / `types/database.ts`** — `getMemoryContentPage` paging read path; message/readAttachment actions consume pages instead of whole rows.
- **`plugin-sql` schema + store (new: `memoryTextSegments`)** — generation-addressed segments with revision fencing: `createMemory` publishes segments with a bounded marker, `updateMemory` replaces the generation and retires the stale one, large-to-small replacement retires the descriptor, deletion cascades; small content stays inline (fallback path returns null pages); large attachment text without an id or with duplicate ids is rejected.
- **Real-runtime suites (new)** — 10 real PGlite tests: parent-first publication, paging with revision fencing, reassembly across restart, atomic generation replacement, legacy large-unsegmented row flagging, owner-bound attachment paging, access-context probe coverage, rollback atomicity.

## Key invariants

- Pages are revision-fenced: a reader can never reassemble content mixing two generations.
- Generation replacement is atomic and retires the prior generation — stale segments are never served after an update.
- Legacy large unsegmented rows are flagged, not silently repaged; small rows pass through inline.

## Test-lane disclosure

Nine of the ten new plugin-sql tests live in `*.real.test.ts` files, which the PR vitest lane deliberately excludes (`plugins/plugin-sql/src/vitest.config.ts`, #10104) — they run on the post-merge lane (`VITEST_LANE=post-merge` / `TEST_LANE=post-merge`) and in the captures below. The pre-merge green checks therefore reflect the non-real suites (core unit + surface + probe tests), not the real-PGlite fencing behavior; see the backend-logs capture for the real-suite evidence. The post-merge lane does execute plugin-sql real suites.

Closes #25141

Introduces a durable, lossless content-manifest shard ledger so progressive content (trajectories and other paginated corpora) survives restarts and concurrent writers without truncation or orphaned shards.

Investigation doc: `docs/design/context-content/25141-manifest-shard-persistence-investigation.md` (included).

## What changes

- **`packages/core/src/runtime/content-manifest-ledger.ts` (new)** — generation-addressed shard writes with a rolling `chainSha256` over shard body bytes; `ManifestHead.contentSha256` retention-bound digest (createdAt-free); load-path digest verification with a typed integrity error; deterministic idempotency (content-digest comparison on both write paths); entry-level revision containment (`entryIdentity` = kind + reference + normalized revision, range-coverage superset check).
- **`packages/core/src/types/content-manifest-shards.ts` (new)** — shard type contracts: fixed-point byteLength measure, `CONTENT_MANIFEST_SHARD_DEFAULT_ENTRIES=64`, >maxBytes typed rejection.
- **`plugin-sql/src/base.ts`** — SQL CAS split into insert-only (`onConflictDoNothing`) vs conditional-update arms (ABA-safe); loser sweeps own generation; delete/clear sweeps ledger rows (`RETURNING id`).
- **`plugin-inmemorydb` + core `inMemoryAdapter`** — atomic CAS via document mutation lock; `compareAndSwapCache` contract with base-class default for structural third-party adapters.
- **`TrajectoriesService` / agent prune paths** — prune-delete guard via `contentManifestLedgerKeys` wired into `discard` and `pruneOldTrajectories` (RETURNING-id cleanup).
- **Tests** — 48 core ledger/shard unit tests, 11 real PGlite integration + restart tests (deterministic injected-clock runs, entry-level revision containment vectors, restart superset/grown-ranges manifest assertions).

## Key invariants

- A restart never publishes a shrinking manifest that silently drops recorded entries: the restart suite asserts superset/grown-ranges (a shrinking 5-replaces-9 manifest was found by a stash control and fixed).
- Idempotency compares content digests, not wall-clock timestamps; writer races resolve CAS-safe with loser-side sweep of its own generation.
- Load-path verifies the chain digest and fails with a typed integrity error rather than serving truncated content.

# Risks

Medium. Enrollment advances sandbox schedule state and creates durable backup work. A defect could skip due work, duplicate queue entries, cross a source occurrence, or strand a shard. The repository therefore uses one atomic transaction, frozen per-shard cohort authority, bounded disjoint candidate frontiers, exact source revalidation, deterministic organization locking, and replay-safe insertion.

# What does this PR do?

- Leases one of 64 durable enrollment shards with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, preferring incomplete cohorts.
- Freezes the database cutoff, snapshot xid, RPO, cohort identity, and keyset cursor for resumable enrollment.
- Selects three disjoint due frontiers, each bounded at `limit + 1`, then globally orders and caps the result.
- Revalidates active organization lifecycle and exact sandbox/node occurrence authority before mutation.
- Atomically advances `next_backup_at`, enrollment cursors, queued `schedule_capture` / `reserve_capture` work, and shard progress.
- Inserts exact replay identities with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`; queued rows begin with attempts `0`, no lease, and no claim proof.
- Performs database admission mutations only. It has no provider, provisioning, capacity, autoscale, or restore dependency.

# What this PR does

- Keeps browser and native Cloud request deadlines active through response body/decode work, propagates caller cancellation without replacing its reason/cause, and rechecks the absolute wall clock immediately before every transport dispatch.
- Starts the six-minute Dedicated startup deadline at `ensurePersonalDedicatedEliza()` entry, not after Personal/quote/activation preflight. Personal GET, quote GET, activation POST, bodies, reconciliation, and cutover polling all consume the same remaining budget.
- Proves a `359999 -> 360000` dispatch crossover sends zero late POSTs and that aggregate preflight + quote + ambiguous activation + cutover settles by 360000 ms with no late effects.
- Distinguishes direct session verification outcomes: only authoritative 401/403 may request reauthentication. Body stalls, malformed responses, 5xx, and transport failures retain the token and surface a transient retry outcome.
- Makes required-client-auth mounted Steward login fail closed on transient verification, matching Android behavior, so first-run join/provisioning cannot continue on an unverified retained token. Optional login UI still retains the token and shows a retry message.
- Recognizes retained Dedicated states without replay: `pending`, `provisioning`, and `running` reattach with zero activation POST; `error`, `stopped`, and `sleeping` allow exactly one fresh quote-bound same-target activation; unknown state and target mismatch fail closed.
- Uses stable `ElizaError` codes with sanitized context for invalid activation, unknown quote/status, and target mismatch.
- Guards Personal identity recovery diagnostics so a rejected diagnostic sink cannot mask the original typed recovery failure.
- Records a single fixed payload-free warning when that diagnostic sink rejects, while preserving the original typed failure; the J2/J4/J7 catch boundaries carry explicit repository-policy rationales.
- Retains privacy-safe counters only; no credentials, response payloads, account identifiers, or billing secrets are logged.

# Review remediation receipts

- `discussion_r3873629448`: response metadata now survives body rejection and timeout, including status, URL, response headers, and parsed `Retry-After`. Authoritative 401/403 verification does not consume an untrusted error body and clears only the same-current token; rejecting/stalled 409, 423, and 503 bodies retain metadata for bounded retry classification. The retained-target regression proves zero activation replay.
- `discussion_r3873629450`: a usable stored Steward token no longer claims an OAuth popup before silent provisioning. Token-less OAuth still claims synchronously under the user gesture, and an indefinitely pending Dedicated activation keeps `window.open` at zero calls.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

This draft introduces the S1 durable substrate for one-shot sandbox replacement attempts:

- a tenant-scoped attempt schema that freezes caller attempt identity, activation/lifecycle authority, backup/restore authority, complete S0 node/SSH placement identity, monotonic locator enrichment, and byte-identical receipts;
- a global partial unique fence on `(organization_id, agent_id)` while an attempt is `in_flight_unresolved` or `provider_succeeded`;
- a per-generation partial unique fence that additionally retains `lifecycle_committed` history for the same activation generation;
- transaction-composable repository operations for start, intent, locator stages, provider success, lifecycle adoption, cleanup proof, and primary reads, with typed conflict/not-found/validation errors;
- adversarial PGlite coverage for real rotation, concurrency, rollback, replay, cleanup/start serialization, terminal immutability, tenant isolation, malformed authority, and non-expiring unresolved attempts.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature: a bounded backend persistence substrate for later #22947 runtime slices.

Replaces the event-only Slack membership handlers with permission-aware, account-scoped membership evidence from the Slack Web API, published to the canonical `MembershipService` contract.

## What changes

- **`src/membership.ts` (new, 233 lines)** — snapshot/delta evidence engine: `conversations.members` paging, sender renewals, join/leave deltas, multi-account identity scoping, typed error classification.

## Key invariants

- Partial/failed/intent-missing evidence reports `unavailable`/`incomplete`; it never implies removals.
- Per-account scoping: one account's degrade never marks another account's evidence stale.
- `conversations.replies` ordering is earliest-first (parent-first) per Slack docs — the harness previously asserted the reverse, which was a production bug fixed with a RED control.

ed:Tb88,## Cause

The Android and live-voice evidence paths could publish device serials, raw logcat/command diagnostics, provider/model/backend/provenance values, and captured physical/system audio through logs or uploaded artifacts. The `always()` upload paths could also expose partially written evidence, and the existing voice matrix v1 schema still carried raw diagnostic fields.

## Resolution

- project Android workflow output through a closed, allowlisted status/code boundary; keep serials, logcat, screenshots, raw console output, and runner state private
- bind published Android evidence to the exact revision/build identity and SHA-256 manifest; emit black, audio-free video only
- move voice evidence to `eliza_voice_live_matrix_v2` and remove raw host/filter/probe/child diagnostics
- derive public voice audio only as a fixed 997 Hz synthetic tone from duration; publish black video plus that projected tone, never captured mic/system audio
- stage, verify, and atomically rename the exact manifest-bound Android and voice artifact sets into absent destinations
- reject symlink destinations and parent substitution; pin and revalidate publication ancestry, parent, and staging identities
- keep the hosted Android bootstrap at `android/logs/` while atomically publishing its allowlisted proof at `android/evidence/`
- use the canonical per-user runner temp directory as the explicit Windows publication trust boundary, with a fresh absent default child
- isolate workflow roots by run id/attempt and make teardown sequential and bounded
